kanbanCards.html: BUG (operator hit LIVE on .6, mid-session after agent work / sub-agent spawn). The Windows input mode gets CORRUPTED mid-session and codex does not repair it: [I/[O (focus reports) flood as literal text AND full input breaks -- Backspace echoes as a space instead of deleting, Enter does NOT submit + Escape does NOT stop the agent, and special keys (e.g. Page Down) are inputted as their literal CHARACTER instead of performing the action. I.e. the terminal drops out of codex raw/VT-input mode and keys are no longer parsed as events. The .5 focus-leak fix is INSUFFICIENT (operator did not thoroughly test .5; bug may have existed there too). .7 inherits .6 so it carries this too.

ROOT CAUSE (source-settled, read-only investigation 2026-06-13, .ralph/investigations/codex-focus-leak-recur-after-subagent-v6/findings.md). Q0: codex .6 does NOT leave ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT on by default -- startup clears it (tui.rs:1365-1379) and codex-owned restores keep it cleared (tui.rs:414-449,1351-1361,1384-1397), so the .5 fix on THAT bit works. THE GAP IS BROADER: the raw-mode bits (ENABLE_LINE_INPUT | ENABLE_ECHO_INPUT | ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT) can be corrupted mid-session and are NEVER re-asserted before normal event reads (event_stream.rs:178-220; crossterm raw bits at crossterm/src/terminal/sys/windows.rs:17-39). That explains ALL symptoms (line-input/echo back on -> backspace echoes + Enter cooked; processed-input + focus reporting -> [I/[O + special keys as literal chars). NOTE: no source-citable built-in sub-agent path re-enables the mode -- codex built-in spawn is IN-PROCESS (multi_agents/spawn.rs:79-139), not an inherited-console OS child; so whatever corrupts the mode, the robust finding is codex must SELF-HEAL the full input mode before event reads. FIX: a Windows full-input-mode guard in tui.rs that re-asserts the complete expected console mode (raw bits cleared + VT-input cleared + focus reporting off) before event reads / on every event-stream resume; + stop enabling xterm focus reporting on Windows unless needed.

NOT /goal-specific: the reprint happens because the LIVE VIEWPORT actively RE-RENDERS while/after the resume history prints, and each re-render RE-EMITS all committed history. ## The fix (codex-side only; NO crossterm fork)
Root cause (verified, committed): on WINDOWS, codex inherits `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT` on stdin (Windows Terminal's default console mode), so the terminal delivers VT-input-style `KEY_EVENT_RECORD`s. crossterm's Windows parser only maps `Esc` when `wVirtualKeyCode == VK_ESCAPE`; in the VT-input case the `ESC` leader arrives with `wVirtualKeyCode == 0`, falls into the control-char branch, `get_char_for_key()` returns `None` (ESC dropped), while the tail bytes (`[`, `O`, `I`, `6`, `~`) survive as `KeyCode::Char` — so focus reports leak as `[O[I` and PageDown leaks as `[6~`. Windows-only (Linux/macOS use the VT byte-stream path that parses correctly).

THE FIX (codex-side, in `codex-rs/tui/src/tui.rs`): before `enable_raw_mode()`, on Windows, clear the inherited `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT` bit on `STD_INPUT_HANDLE` (so the console delivers classic key-event records that crossterm's Windows parser decodes correctly — VK_ESCAPE→Esc, VK_NEXT→PageDown). Save the prior input mode and RESTORE only that VT-input bit on restore/exit so `RestoreMode::{Full,KeepRaw}` semantics stay intact (do not clobber other mode bits the restore path manages).

Read the committed design note (on main): `.ralph/investigations/codex-tui-focus-event-leak/fix-design.md` — it has the exact subtlety resolution, the file:line landing site in `tui.rs`, the save/restore approach, the `RestoreMode::KeepRaw` constraint, and the bg-notification non-regression check. Implement EXACTLY what the design specifies; if you find a concrete reason to deviate, note it in your report.

## CRITICAL non-regression
The background-process-notification feature depends on focus reporting + `terminal_focused`. Your fix must NOT disable `EnableFocusChange` and must NOT regress focus-event delivery — it only changes the Windows INPUT console mode so the focus/PageDown VT sequences are decoded as proper key/focus events instead of leaking. Evaluation complete (findings.md, 18.6KB). Verdict: VIABLE-WITH-WORK, and the answer splits by codex's TWO roles. ROLE A (happy-cli programmatic engine, app-server over loopback ws): viable-with-work — opencode ships a documented headless server (HTTP + SSE + OpenAPI SDK), and crucially NATIVE GitHub Copilot transport (OAuth device flow, live /models, header injection), which ERASES the codex fork's single largest patch class (the fork is literally named …-copilot-api.1). WINS (opencode already has what we patched into codex): native Copilot (biggest), .claude/.agents skills compat, headless SDK, npm plugins + remote-MCP-OAuth, native background subagents, no chatgpt.com remote-control to disable. shipManifest.summary:
crews v3.14.0 — a two-layer, on-demand engine plugin provisioner. A lead/bookkeeper who notices a member's engine is missing a plugin (e.g. a codex member that can only see crews, not ralph) can now install/refresh it with one command and get a structured verdict telling them whether the blocked member must be respawned to actually see the new plugin.

Layer 1 is a tested CLI subcommand `install-plugin <plugin> --engine <copilot|claude|codex> [--version] [--marketplace] [--dry-run] [--exact]` that thinly wraps each engine's native plugin CLI and emits a structured JSON verdict {status: installed|no-op|upgraded|failed, restartRequired, currentThreadUsable}. Layer 2 is a thin generated /crews-install-plugin skill plus a read-only list-plugins discovery companion. Durable logic lives in lib/plugin-provisioning/ (index/version/source/command-runner + per-engine adapters). The codex adapter is LOCAL-SOURCE ONLY (dodging the git-marketplace auto-upgrade corruption bug) with cache-lag refresh; restart handling is REPORT-ONLY (never auto-restarts a running member). 8 stories, Phase-4 10 findings fixed/1 dismissed; 295/295 tests green. This is the provisioning prerequisite for switching the default crews member engine from copilot to codex.

shipManifest.summary: Lead-driven fix shipped as crews v3.8.0. Windows file-scanner pressure (Defender real-time scan + Search indexer) momentarily locks the rapidly-rewritten .crews lock / manifest.json files; libuv surfaces this as code="UNKNOWN" (errno -4094, the "unmappable Win32 error" bucket) rather than the EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY that the v3.5.0 EPERM-recovery already tolerated. The unretried UNKNOWN crashed a lead listener (raw throw out of acquireLock's fs.openSync(lockPath,"wx")) and terminated two brainstorm members on their FIRST heartbeat failure (consecutiveFailures=0) on 2026-06-06 (crews.log: listener-eperm-terminate reason=heartbeat-non-transient errCode=UNKNOWN). Two-predicate fix: hooks/locks.js isTransientLockOpenError adds UNKNOWN so acquireLock retries-with-jitter instead of throwing out of withManifestLock (predicate now exported for unit testing); hooks/safe-io.js TRANSIENT_RENAME_ERRORS adds UNKNOWN -- the single Set consumed by BOTH renameSyncWithRetry (atomic-write rename retry) AND classifyHeartbeatError -> decideHeartbeatAction (heartbeat continue-vs-terminate). The heartbeat classifier stays gated on syscall==="rename", so a non-rename UNKNOWN still terminates -- the v3.5.0 narrow-predicate invariant is preserved; the lock-open UNKNOWN is absorbed at the acquireLock retry layer so it never reaches the heartbeat decider as a raw throw. 5 new regression cases (16 -> 21 in listener-eperm-recovery.test.js): UNKNOWN-on-rename continues to the cap, UNKNOWN-on-non-rename non-transient, renameSyncWithRetry retries through UNKNOWN, locks.isTransientLockOpenError accepts UNKNOWN while genuine errors are not swallowed, and an end-to-end acquireLock retry through an injected UNKNOWN lock-open. Rubber-duck reviewed (no blocking issues; the temp-file writeFileSync seam is an acceptable-to-defer theoretical gap -- unique-per-call fresh temp, uncontended). Full crews suite 279/279. Version 3.7.0 -> 3.8.0 (3 plugin.json + 3 marketplace indexes + version-stamp test). copilot plugin update applied live (crews 3.7.0 -> 3.8.0, 24 skills) so this session's own listener now tolerates UNKNOWN.

Context - bug confirmed by operator 2026-06-04T22:55Z:

Copilot members run and emit assistant turns (visible in their wt.exe tab; they spawn child processes, edit files, etc.), but `list-members` shows for them: `lastTurnAt: null`, `lastKind: null`, `lastSeq: 0`. This breaks operator visibility -- `/list-members` and `list-members` JSON show 'never turned' status for members doing real work.

The bug becomes invisible AFTER the member emits its first `kind=done` report (then a subsequent agentStop fires the manifest-update path and populates the fields). Earlier 2026-06-04T14:50Z I wrongly archived this thinking it was bookkeeper observation error. The v5.50 ship that 'proved' the manifest works was a confounder, not a counterexample -- the manifest only updates after kind=done.

Known working path: heartbeat update path (touchHeartbeat -> markArmed -> writeJsonAtomic) writes `lastHeartbeatAt` fine, even on Copilot. So the file-write infrastructure works; the bug is in WHICH manifest fields the per-turn agentStop path writes.

3 hypotheses to investigate (impl member decides which is right):

1. **agentStop hook isn't firing per assistant turn under autonomous wrapping.** Test: instrument `hooks/copilot-stop.js` to log every invocation to crews.log with timestamp + payload-keys; spawn a small test member that emits 3 progress messages; check log.

2. **agentStop fires but skips the manifest-write.** Look at the manifest-write path in `hooks/stop.js` (or `copilot-stop.js`'s shim into it) -- maybe Copilot's stdin payload shape lacks a field the path expects, causing an early return before the `updateManifest` call that would write `lastTurnAt`/`lastKind`/`lastSummary`/`lastSeq`.

3. **The report-tag parser doesn't recognize the autonomous member's tag emissions.** The autonomous /implement-with-ralph orchestrator may emit tags in a non-canonical position (e.g., not the very last line) and the parser's first-tag-wins or last-line-only logic skips them.

Reference working code: same hooks for Claude members DO update `lastTurnAt`/`lastKind`/`lastSummary`/`lastSeq` per turn (operator-validated this earlier 2026-06-04 sessions). So the bug is Copilot-specific.

Fix scope (impl member decides):

- **Option A**: instrument + log first to identify which hypothesis is right (~30min discovery).
- **Option B**: apply the fix once root cause is clear (could be ~5-30 lines depending on which hypothesis).
- **Option C**: add a test in `tests/copilot-stop.test.js` or `tests/copilot-shim.test.js` that simulates an agentStop with a progress tag and asserts the manifest fields update.

Acceptance criteria:

1. After spawning a fresh Copilot member that emits a progress message, `list-members` shows non-null `lastTurnAt` + populated `lastKind` + populated `lastSummary` + non-zero `lastSeq` WITHOUT requiring a terminal `kind=done` report.
2. New regression test in `tests/copilot-*.test.js` covers the progress-tag manifest-update path.
3. Telemetry log line added: `manifest-turn-update name=<name> crew=<crew> kind=<kind> seq=<N>` on every successful update so operators can grep for it.
4. Same fix works for ALL kind values (progress, done, question, blocked).
5. Claude path remains unchanged + green.
6. AGENTS.md section added under crews v3.5 follow-on entry documenting the fix + the operator-visibility motivation.
7. 5-file version stamp bump if shipping as own release (likely v3.5.1 or v3.6.0).

Out of scope:

- Architectural refactor of the agentStop manifest-update path (v2-deferred).
- Member-side recovery wrapper (separate bug; only relevant if recovery is also missing).

At ship time, the lead will need to rebase the second-to-ship topic branch onto the first's main (small rebase: plugin.json + AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG.md + marketplace indexes). No code-level conflicts -- impl-codex-engine-full touches hooks/actors.js, lib/session-env.js, briefing/, new .codex-plugin/, new hooks/codex-*.js -- while this fix targets hooks/copilot-stop.js or hooks/stop.js manifest-update path.

Context — bug is HOT and recurring:

Observed 5+ times in a single bookkeeper session today (2026-06-04) on this Windows dev box. The lead-side listener subprocess crashes with EPERM during the atomic-rename step in writeJsonAtomic:

```
Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename 'D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.crews\crews\ralph-pipeline\leads\overview-bookkeeper\manifest.json.<pid>.<hex>.tmp' -> 'D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.crews\crews\ralph-pipeline\leads\overview-bookkeeper\manifest.json'
    at Object.renameSync (node:fs:1033:11)
    at writeJsonAtomic (.../crews/hooks/mailbox.js:180:12)
    at writeManifest (.../crews/hooks/actors.js:389:3)
    at updateManifest (.../crews/hooks/actors.js:399:10)
    at touchHeartbeat (.../crews/hooks/actors.js:839/867)
    at markArmed (.../crews/hooks/listener-protocol.js:185:18)
    at Timeout._onTimeout (.../crews/lib/listener-loop.js:155:7)
```

Member-side ALSO observed (sender impl-worktree-conditional-narrow reported: "Listener crashed on mailbox lock contention. Re-arming. Listener re-armed.") — members have an apparent recovery wrapper; lead-side does NOT.

Known context per crews AGENTS.md:

- v1.4.1 shipped a retry shim wrapping `renameSync` for EBUSY/EACCES/EPERM, up to 3 attempts with 100ms × attempt backoff, using synchronous Atomics.wait-based sleep. This is the existing protection.
- v1.6.0 shipped `isTransientLockOpenError` for `O_EXCL` lock-open failures with retry inside the existing lock-acquisition loop.

Hypothesis (the impl member should verify):

1. **Retry exhaustion under Defender pressure**: 3 attempts × 100ms = 300ms ceiling may be too tight when Microsoft Defender real-time scan briefly holds a read handle on the destination. Today's session had 5+ crashes inside ~3 hours — high enough rate to suggest the budget is insufficient on this dev box.
2. **Heartbeat path missing wrap**: the v1.4.1 wrap is in `writeJsonAtomic`, but maybe `markArmed` or some sibling path has a separate rename that's NOT wrapped.
3. **Auto-recovery asymmetry**: members appear to auto-recover ("Listener re-armed." message in body), but leads do not. The lead-side listener-loop heartbeat timer crashes the entire process. Member-side may have a try/catch around the heartbeat call.

Fix scope (the impl member decides which based on investigation):

- **Option A — extend retry budget**: increase v1.4.1's 3 attempts × 100ms to 10 attempts × exponential backoff (100ms, 200ms, 400ms, 800ms, ...) capped at e.g. 5s. Add telemetry log line (crews.log) when retry succeeds after N >= 2 attempts, so operators can grep for high retry rates. Tradeoff: longer worst-case latency on a real corruption.

- **Option B — wrap any unwrapped path**: audit all callers of `renameSync` in hooks/ and ensure they go through `writeJsonAtomic` (or an equivalent retry-protected helper). If `markArmed` or `touchHeartbeat` has a bypass, route through.

- **Option C — lead-side auto-recovery**: catch the EPERM-exhausted exception in `listener-loop.js`'s heartbeat timer, log it, and continue the loop instead of crashing the process. Member-side already does this (per the seq-3 evidence in today's session: "Listener crashed on mailbox lock contention. Re-arming."). Tradeoff: a heartbeat write failure means the manifest hasn't been touched, so the lead may appear stale; need to re-attempt the write on the next tick rather than silent-skip.

Likely the right fix is A + C combined (extend budget so it rarely exhausts; if it DOES exhaust, recover instead of crash).

Acceptance criteria:

1. The v1.4.1 retry shim's attempt count and backoff are tunable AND verified to be appropriate for the observed Defender pressure on the dev box.
2. Listener process survives an EPERM rename exhaustion event WITHOUT crashing (auto-recovery path lands).
3. New test in `tests/listener-eperm-recovery.test.js` (or similar) simulates an EPERM exhaustion (e.g., mock renameSync to throw EPERM N+1 times) and asserts the listener-loop continues running + the next heartbeat tick succeeds + a `listener-eperm-retry-exhausted` log line lands in crews.log.
4. Member-side auto-recovery (currently in evidence per today's session) is documented in the existing recovery path so the lead-side fix can mirror it.
5. Telemetry log line added: when retry succeeds after N >= 2 attempts, append `listener-eperm-retry-recovered name=<name> crew=<crew> attempts=<N> elapsed=<ms>` to crews.log. When retry exhausts AND lead-side recovery activates, append `listener-eperm-retry-exhausted-recovered name=<name> crew=<crew>`.
6. AGENTS.md section added for the new behavior (v1.4.1 follow-up or v3.5.0 entry depending on scope).
7. 5-file version stamp bump via scripts/bump-version.js if shipped as own release.
8. Manual smoke: bookkeeper lead listener survives at least 30 min of session use without crashing.

Out of scope:

- Architectural refactor (e.g., abandoning the rename-based atomic write for an OS-specific approach like fsync+rename on Unix vs. ReplaceFileW on Windows). v2-deferred.
- Server-side / mobile-app changes — bug is entirely in crews plugin Windows-side.
- Member-side recovery audit beyond verifying the existing behavior is what we observe.

Context:

Operator requested 2026-06-04: add codex as a 3rd engine in crews `/spawn-member --engine codex|claude|copilot`, alongside the existing Claude (v1.0) and Copilot CLI (v1.3.0) integrations. Today crews can spawn a Claude or Copilot member; we want a codex member that participates in the same crew protocol (mailbox, listener-arm, kind-tag report footers, lead/member roles, peers, threads, stop-member, resume-crew, etc.).

Reference work (Copilot port, v1.3.0):

The v1.3.0 ship is documented in `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/AGENTS.md` under `## v1.3.0 GitHub Copilot CLI support` and was a 12+ story plan. Touch points it covered:

1. `manifest.engine` field enum extended from `claude` to `claude | copilot` (default `claude`). Used by `/resume-crew` to dispatch the correct launcher.
2. `buildLauncherCommand(engine, options)` in `hooks/actors.js` is the single source of truth. Claude path emits `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --name '<n>' --plugin-dir '<r>' '<prompt>'`; Copilot path emits `copilot --name '<n>' --allow-all --plugin-dir '<r>' -i '<prompt>'` (Copilot has no default positional command, so prompt comes via `-i`; `--allow-all` skips tool/dir/url prompts).
3. `.copilot-plugin/` overlay shipped: `.github/plugin/plugin.json` (Copilot plugin manifest), `.github/plugin/hooks.json` (declares `sessionStart`/`agentStop`/`preToolUse`/`userPromptSubmit`/`postToolUse` — camelCase, distinct from Claude's PascalCase), 4 shim entry points (`hooks/copilot-{session-start,stop,pre-tool-use,user-prompt-submit}.js`), `.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md` × 21 (kebab-prefixed slash form, e.g. `/crews-status`, because Copilot doesn't support the `crews:<command>` colon namespace).
4. `hooks/copilot-shim.js` is a pure stdin/stdout shape translator. Copilot delivers `{ sessionId, toolName, toolArgs }` (toolArgs sometimes JSON-string, sometimes object); Claude expects `{ session_id, tool_name, tool_input (object) }`. Shim writes BOTH `{ decision, reason }` AND `{ permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason }` on block paths so whichever Copilot honors fires.
5. Briefing variants: `hooks/briefing/template.js::renderListenerArmSection(ctx)` branches on `ctx.engine`. Claude emits `Bash tool ... run_in_background: true`; Copilot emits `bash tool ... mode: "async"` (Copilot's async-shell syntax differs). Copilot also references `/crews-review-mail` (kebab) instead of `/crews:review-mail` (colon) in the resume-protocol section.
6. Resume path: `/resume-crew --confirm` reads `manifest.engine` inside `repairManifestForResume` and dispatches the launcher accordingly. Transcript-existence fallback uses `manifest.transcriptPath` for Claude (`~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl`) but derives `~/.copilot/session-state/<sessionId>/events.jsonl` for Copilot (Copilot's own session-state directory). When transcript missing, both engines fall back to bare relaunch + full continuation briefing.
7. `readSessionEnv()` in `hooks/lib/session-env.js` reads the agent-session env: when both `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID` are present, picks Copilot if `COPILOT_CLI=1` is also set, else Claude. Tiebreak markers: `CLAUDECODE=1` / `COPILOT_CLI=1`.
8. Test surface: `tests/copilot-shim.test.js`, `tests/copilot-review-fixes.test.js`, integration tests, briefing-discoverability test classifier flips, golden file regens.

Gaps to investigate for the codex port (the brainstorm should fan out on these):

1. **Codex CLI invocation shape**: what's the launcher command? `codex --name '<n>' --plugin-dir '<r>' '<prompt>'`? Does codex have an `--allow-all` analog? Does it have an `-i` flag for non-positional prompt? What about `--dangerously-skip-permissions`?

2. **Codex hook system**: does codex have hooks at all, or do we have to bolt on a wrapper? If codex hooks exist, what are the event names? Are they PascalCase / camelCase / snake_case? What's the stdin payload shape? Does codex honor `decision: block` from a hook, or does the shim need a different mechanism (e.g., post-tool denial)?

3. **Codex session lifecycle**: where does codex store its session state? `~/.codex/sessions/<id>/`? What's in there — JSONL events, a manifest, both? Does codex have a `--resume <id>` flag? What does `--name` do (display label vs session id seed)?

4. **Codex slash command registry**: how does codex discover and dispatch slash commands? Is there a `.codex-plugin/` analog? Does codex use colon namespace, kebab, snake, or something else? What's the slash-command discovery surface (filesystem-based vs registry-based)?

5. **Codex skill / agent discovery**: does codex have a Skill tool analog? Or are agents discovered via a registry file (the existing codex AGENTS.md hints at this)? What about codex's `task()` tool (sub-agent spawn) — does that interact with crews?

6. **Codex bash / shell tool semantics**: does codex have an async-bash mode analog to Claude's `run_in_background: true` and Copilot's `mode: "async"`? If not, how do we arm a long-running listener subprocess from inside a codex turn?

7. **Codex transcript format**: what does the events.jsonl analog look like? Is there a `tool.execution_start` / `system.notification` analog the bg-gate detector can scan? Or do we need a codex-specific bg-detection signal source (per the crews AGENTS.md v3.1.0 detector-extension guidance)?

8. **3-way env tiebreak**: extend `readSessionEnv()` to handle CODEX session id env vars (whatever they are — `CODEX_SESSION_ID`? `CODEX_AGENT_SESSION_ID`?). Tiebreak when all 3 are set.

9. **Launcher env scrub**: existing scrubs (Copilot launcher removes Claude session env, Claude launcher removes Copilot session env) need a 3-way variant: codex launcher removes Claude + Copilot session env.

10. **`.codex-plugin/` overlay scope**: do we ship 21 codex-flavored SKILL.md files? Or does codex's plugin model use a different discovery surface (e.g., agent-registry config)? Are the per-skill `<plugin>:<command>` colon mirrors needed?

11. **Copilot port lessons that DON'T apply**: Copilot port specifically dealt with Copilot's `ask_user` snake_case (v1.3.12) and Copilot's per-intent OSC title rewriter (v1.8.12) and Copilot's `wt.exe` interactions. Codex likely has its own pile of analogous engine-specific gotchas.

12. **Tab title**: codex displays its agent name where? wt.exe tab title? Console window title? Both? Does codex have an env var to disable per-turn title rewriting (analog to `COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE`)?

13. **Testing strategy**: how do we write the equivalent of `tests/copilot-shim.test.js` for codex? Can we mock codex's hook stdin shape? Is there a codex test fixture analog?

Related tracked tasks the brainstorm should consider:

- `codex-app-server-daemon-codexu-integration` [brainstorm-first, JUST FILED] — daemon-side integration. Separate but adjacent.
- `crews-roles-and-direct-operator-channel` [brainstorm-first] — 3-party role redesign. Engine-orthogonal.
- `codex-local-build` [brainstorm-first] — make codex Rust workspace compile on Windows. NOT a prereq but maybe useful context (a codex member would invoke the codex binary, which the codex-local-build addresses).
- `agent-comms` [tracked, plan, blocked] — same-daemon comm scope intersects.

Deliverable:

Multi-lens brainstorm (Codex feasibility + Copilot product-reality + Devil's advocate + Claude synthesis) → `selected-direction.md` ready for `/plan-with-ralph --from-brainstorm`. The synthesized direction should:

- Pick the realistic single-cycle subset of the v1.3.0-comparable scope.
- Identify which gaps are pure-port (just translate from Copilot's pattern) vs. genuinely-novel (codex has no analog).
- Identify which gaps can be DEFERRED (codex member ships without slash commands? without skills? minimal-viable codex member that only does plain prose + mailbox + report-tag?).
- Identify the engine-asymmetric tests we'd need (and which existing copilot-shim tests can serve as templates).
- Identify which features of the existing Claude/Copilot paths would need adjustment to accommodate a 3-way (vs. binary) engine choice (e.g., `readSessionEnv` tiebreak, launcher env scrub, briefing renderer branches).
- Estimate whether the port is one impl ship (12-story plan, ~1-2 sessions like v1.3.0) or needs to be split across 2-3 ships (e.g., "minimal codex member" first, then "codex-flavored skills" later, then "codex-bg-detection" later).

DO NOT try to ship without an explicit decision on the deferred scope — every deferred capability needs a written rationale so a future ship can pick it up without re-discovering.

Context:

Observed on TWO independent machines + sessions:

1. **codexu v5.50 impl member (our session, 2026-06-04)**: `impl-worktree-conditional-narrow` sent seq 1 + seq 2 with IDENTICAL `kind=done` bodies (10 commits on ralph/.../tip 5bff9938; 9/9 stories pass; ...) and seq 3 = `kind=progress` with body "Listener crashed on mailbox lock contention. Re-arming. Listener re-armed. Impl is complete. Awaiting any lead follow-up via the mailbox. Idle." Three envelopes; one substantive.

2. **operator-reported other-PC session (seval-540475 crew, 2026-06-04)**: `summarizer-behavior` member sent 3 duplicate ack envelopes — all just status pings with no new substantive content. Lead's analysis attributed it to: listener wake-ups (from lead arm calls, fs.watch events, nag deliveries) force new turns; members must emit kind tag every turn (v1.8.1 lead exemption does NOT extend to members); with nothing substantive to say, member emits minimal `done` or `progress` stubs like "Listener re-armed" or "Listener already active".

Reportedly documented as a known design quirk: `plugins/crews/docs/architecture-refactor.md` option D ("side-channel listener queue") flagged it as a deferred 2.0 redesign of the "listener-exit-as-wakeup → new turn → required kind footer" model. Worth verifying this reference matches the canonical refactor doc before scoping mitigation work.

Why it matters:

- **Lead-side noise**: every redundant envelope creates a mailbox entry the lead has to consume + acknowledge via the STRICT-ACK contract. The dedup work goes to whoever's reviewing (operator or bookkeeper agent).
- **Compounding effect**: every consumed entry advances the cursor; the lead's `review-mail` has to scroll through more rows to find the substantive ones. With many members, this noise dominates the lead's mailbox.
- **Listener-arm pressure**: as a side effect of needing to ack the noise, the lead burns extra turns on review-mail + ack tags. The listener arm churn (from earlier sessions where re-arms happened every empty timeout cycle) was an analogous waste; the lead-protected `Don't re-arm on every empty timeout cycle` rule from codexu AGENTS.md (codified 2026-06-03) is the parallel discipline.

v1.x mitigation candidates the brainstorm should evaluate:

1. **Lead-side dedup on review-mail**: when 2+ consecutive consumed entries from the same sender have identical or near-identical bodies (within a configurable similarity threshold), collapse them into one displayed row with `count=N`. Cursor advances past all of them as if reviewed individually. Surface: `hooks/commands/review-mail.js::formatReviewMailEntry` + a new collapse pass. Tradeoff: silent collapse hides genuine duplicate emissions that might indicate a runaway loop; pair with a stderr warning when collapsing > 5 in a single batch.

2. **Source-side suppression**: member's Stop hook detects "would emit kind=done with body identical (or near-identical) to last emitted kind=done" and downgrades to no-op (skip outbox + skip mailbox-history write). Body comparison via hash. Surface: `hooks/stop.js` near the report-tag write site. Tradeoff: re-introduces the "silent-censor" failure mode the v1.4.x crews team explicitly fixed; needs a tight similarity threshold + a stderr warning.

actions.label: Brainstorm
actions.prompt:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Redesign the crews plugin to formalize a 3-party actor model (user ↔ lead ↔ members) with named roles and a defined user-to-member direct-interaction channel.

## Why this matters

Today the crews plugin coordinates 2 parties: leads and members. The human operating the workspace is OUTSIDE the plugin's model — leads relay messages to/from 'the operator' as untyped prose, members never address them directly, and the plugin's hooks/CLI commands have no concept of the human's identity or interaction surface.

This works for the common case but breaks down when:
- A lead's session output addresses 'the operator' generically — members who read shared threads see 'lead said: ask operator about X' but have no canonical way to refer back.
- The human wants to go DIRECTLY to a member's terminal and interact (debug something interactively, demo a UI, type a quick correction). Today this happens out-of-band: the lead never sees the interaction, the member has to ad-hoc explain it later.
- The lead should sometimes ASK the human to take a direct action on a member (e.g. 'the member needs to see your screen' or 'this is a 5-message debugging dance, just go to their terminal'). Today there's no protocol — the lead types prose hoping the human reads it.
- The human has interacted with the member directly and now wants the lead to know what happened. Today they have to manually re-explain to the lead.

## Design axes the brainstorm must pressure-test

### Axis 1 — Naming

For the LEAD's role: keep `lead` (matches existing plugin terminology) vs rename to `orchestrator` / `coordinator` / `scrum-master` / `PM`. `lead` is in active use; rename would be churn unless brainstorm finds a strong reason.

For the USER's role: `operator` (matches my bookkeeper docs) vs `principal` (auth-like) vs `owner` (overloaded) vs `director` vs `human` (too generic). Brainstorm should propose the term that least conflicts with existing plugin / Claude Code / Copilot vocabulary AND is natural in prose ('operator paused the job', 'operator confirmed the merge').

### Axis 2 — Direct user↔member channel mechanism

When the human goes to a member's terminal and types directly, how does the plugin detect + log it?

A. **Nothing.** Trust transcripts. Lead reads member's lastTurnAt + transcriptPath if curious.
B. **Auto-detect via stdin source.** Plugin hooks (PreToolUse / new) flag a turn whose first user message was typed locally (vs delivered via mailbox). Tag the manifest/mailbox-history entry with `via: 'operator-direct'`.
C. **Explicit CLI command.** User runs `crews.js operator-message <member-name> --crew <crew> <text>` from any terminal; plugin posts as an `operator-direct` envelope into the member's inbox AND into the lead's review queue.
D. **Magic prefix in member terminal.** User types `OPERATOR:` or similar as the first line; member's PostToolUse parses and emits an `operator-direct` log entry.
E. **Hybrid.** B + C, with manifest field `lastOperatorDirectAt` derived from whichever fires.

Lens against: latency (how fast does lead know), false-positive risk (B might mis-flag), discoverability (D needs user to remember the prefix), maintenance burden.

### Axis 3 — When should the lead ASK the user to do direct interaction?

Formalize the escalation pattern with named triggers:

- **interactive-debug-needed:** member is in a 3+ turn interactive debugging loop where the lead-relay overhead would dominate.
- **demo-required:** the member needs to show a UI/build/output the human must visually inspect.
- **paused-on-real-time-question:** member's kind=question requires sub-30s response cycle.
- **transcript-too-large-to-relay:** member's context is huge and the lead can't summarize fast enough.

Provide a slash command or envelope kind (e.g. `kind=escalate-to-operator`) that leads emit to BOTH the operator AND the member, signaling 'go talk directly'.

### Axis 4 — How the user notifies the lead about a direct interaction

After the user has gone direct, how do they tell the lead 'I just did X with member Y'?

P. **CLI command:** `crews.js notify-lead --crew <crew> --about <member> <summary>` posts an envelope into the lead's review queue tagged `kind=operator-direct-summary`.
Q. **Member auto-summary on next turn:** the member detects the operator-direct turn(s) just happened, summarizes in its next kind=progress envelope so the lead's normal mail-review surface picks it up.
R. **Lead dashboard recomputes from manifest:** lead's `list-members` command shows a per-member 'lastOperatorDirectAt' column; lead reads transcript on demand.
S. **Silent until lead reviews member transcript:** simplest; least proactive.

### Axis 5 — Lead-side surface

Where/how does the lead see operator-direct events?

- Separate review-mail category (`/crews:review-operator-direct`)
- Merged into existing review-mail with a visual flag
- Dashboard-only (list-members column)
- Both inbox + dashboard
- None — lead asks explicitly

## Constraints / non-negotiable invariants

1. Backwards compatible: existing leads + members without role-aware code keep working. New role surfaces are additive.
2. Cross-engine: claude-code AND copilot hooks need the same surface (per the recent migration audit's lessons).
3. Don't break the v1.6.2 listener-arm gate or v1.7.x sessionId pointer index.
4. Bookkeeper-lead (overview-bookkeeper) should NOT need to change its operating model dramatically — this is additive UX, not a rewrite.
5. Operator notify-CLI commands must work without requiring the operator to know which crew/lead they belong to (auto-discover from cwd, similar to crews.js's existing cwd-discovery patterns).

## Reference + investigation

- Current plugin manifest at `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + same path under `.copilot-plugin/`.
- Hooks at `plugins/crews/hooks/{SessionStart,stop,pre-tool-use,post-tool-use}.js` (+ Copilot mirrors). These are where role-aware logic would live.
- CLI at `plugins/crews/tools/crews.js` — would gain `operator-message`, `notify-lead`, or whatever the brainstorm chooses.
- Mailbox envelope schema at `plugins/crews/hooks/lib/mailbox.js` (or wherever envelope kinds are defined) — would gain new kinds.
- Existing `actor` concept in manifests — review whether adding a 3rd actor role (operator) makes sense or whether operator is fundamentally different (no manifest, no listener, but has identity).
- Auto-memory `feedback_check_mailbox_after_tool_bursts` documents one ad-hoc operator-interaction pattern.

Lenses: feasibility (codex — what's the plumbing actually look like?), product-reality (copilot — would real operators use the CLI?), devil's-advocate (does formalizing this just add overhead operators won't bother with?), simplification (lightest mechanism that captures 80% of the value).

## Deliverable

At end of brainstorm Phase 5, produce `.ralph/brainstorms/crews-roles-and-direct-operator-channel/selected-direction.md` with:

- Recommended naming (lead-role term + operator-role term) with rationale.
- Recommended direct-channel mechanism (A-E or hybrid) with rationale.
- Recommended lead-side surface (separate category / merged / dashboard / etc).
- Concrete escalation triggers (named, with examples) and the slash command / envelope-kind to fire them.
- Concrete user-to-lead notify mechanism (P-S or hybrid).
- Migration story: how existing crews v1.7.x sessions absorb the new model.
- Acceptance criteria for eventual impl.
- Open questions for the planner.

Do NOT chain into /plan-with-ralph. The bookkeeper spawns a fresh plan-crews-roles-and-direct-operator-channel member from the selected-direction.md per phase discipline."

/plan-with-ralph "Retire codexu's gitignored bin/ralph-overview.mjs resolver wrapper, keep cross-engine support (Claude Code + Copilot CLI) for `pnpm sync-ralph-state` / `pnpm overview`.

## Background

Current state on codexu (2026-05-29):
- `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` is a Node resolver wrapper that locates the ralph-overview plugin install dir, then dispatches to the plugin's own `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` via spawn.
- It is **gitignored** (`.gitignore: /bin/` covers it). Earlier this session I added Copilot install-path support (`~/.copilot/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/`) to the wrapper's cascade — that local-machine patch works for THIS machine but doesn't propagate via git.
- The ralph-overview plugin's own `scripts/init-consumer.mjs` writes consumer `package.json` scripts that point directly at `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs` — this only works in Claude Code sessions because `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is auto-injected by Claude. Copilot CLI does NOT export an equivalent var (verified against https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference and https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference 2026-05-29 — Copilot only exports `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI_BINARY_VERSION`, `COPILOT_LOADER_PID`, `COPILOT_RUN_APP`, plus `COPILOT_HOME` for user-config override).

## Goal

`pnpm sync-ralph-state` and `pnpm overview` must work on BOTH engines (Claude Code + Copilot CLI) without:
- Per-developer shell-profile setup (`$RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` exported by every contributor's shell rc — operator burden too high)
- A per-consumer gitignored wrapper that drifts out of sync across machines
- Breaking existing Claude Code workflows that already use the direct `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` path

## Three candidate paths (plan must pick + justify)

### Option A — re-run `overview-init` to regenerate `package.json` scripts in the plugin's modern direct-path form

Writes `"sync-ralph-state": "node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo ."`. Cleanest from the plugin's POV. **Blocker:** breaks under Copilot CLI (no `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`). Would need a parallel Copilot-friendly variant (perhaps a `npm run` cross-shell prelude). Not viable as-is.

### Option B — un-ignore `/bin/` and commit the wrapper with cross-engine support

Local-to-codexu, ships today. Removes the gitignore entry on `/bin/`, commits the existing wrapper with its current cross-engine cascade (Claude install paths + the new Copilot install path I added in-session). Every machine clones a working wrapper. **Downside:** doesn't help OTHER consumers of the ralph-overview plugin who may hit the same Copilot-path gap. Pragmatic short-term fix; doesn't address the root cause.

### Option C — push cross-engine awareness UPSTREAM into `scripts/init-consumer.mjs`

Update the plugin's init flow to emit `package.json` scripts that work on BOTH engines. Three sub-strategies:

   C1. Emit a TINY consumer-side wrapper at install time (essentially what codexu has, but generated + tracked by the plugin's init). Every consumer that runs `overview-init` gets a cross-engine wrapper checked in.
   C2. Emit `package.json` scripts using a cross-shell helper (e.g. `node -e 'import(...).then(...)'` that resolves the plugin path at runtime). Ugly but no wrapper file needed.
   C3. Emit `package.json` scripts that branch on env: `"sync-ralph-state": "node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${COPILOT_HOME:-$HOME/.copilot}/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit}/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo ."`. Bash expansion works on Unix; PowerShell-only Windows users break. Need cross-shell.

Option C is the right architectural answer (helps every consumer) but takes longer (plugin v-bump + adoption cycle).

## Plan must specify

1. **Pick A/B/C** (or hybrid) with clear rationale.
2. **If C:** which sub-strategy (C1/C2/C3) and why; what plugin tests need adding.
3. **Migration story:** if changing the wrapper's location or `package.json` script form, how do existing dev clones absorb the change cleanly (delete old wrapper, regenerate, etc.)?
4. **Cross-engine smoke test:** how to verify `pnpm sync-ralph-state` works under both Claude Code and Copilot CLI before merging. Manual test plan acceptable.
5. **Upstream-feature-request follow-up (Option D, parallel track):** draft a feature request to the GitHub Copilot CLI team proposing a `COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT_<KEBAB-PLUGIN-NAME>` env var or `copilot plugin path <name>` subcommand for parity with Claude Code. Not blocking this task, but a long-term cleaner solution if upstream lands it. The plan should include the draft text.

/plan-with-ralph "Add hard-terminate capability to crews stop-member so the lead can kill a no-longer-needed member's per-tab child process WITHOUT killing the wt.exe server (which would close all sibling tabs) and WITHOUT the soft ack-and-shutdown round-trip via stop-request envelope.

## Why

The current `stop-member` (in `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/commands/stop-member.js` and CLI mirror `tools/stop-member.js`) is a soft authorization:

1. Sets `manifest.shutdownRequested = true` and `manifest.listenerState = exited`
2. Appends a `stop-request` envelope to the member's mailbox
3. The member's next turn reads the stop-request, emits a `kind=done` ack turn
4. Member's Stop hook permits the turn to end; Copilot/Claude session may then exit

Observed cost (2026-05-29 smoke-test, validated): for every clean stop, the bookkeeper-lead receives TWO `kind=done` envelopes from the same member — first the task-completion done, then the stop-acknowledgement done. The second one is pure overhead: no useful work, just 'ok, dying.' The lead must review it (mid-turn nag fires, listener re-arms, etc.) — burning lead-side model invocations too. For an autonomous bookkeeper running dozens of members per day, this is a real tax.

Operator intent: when a member is no longer needed (the common case after a kind=done task report), HARD-TERMINATE the per-member child process tree AND force the tab to visually close. No envelope, no ack round-trip, no second model invocation, no orphaned 'process exited' tab placeholder. **Empirical 2026-05-29: operator observed that in prior smoke-test runs, the tab persisted open with no PowerShell inside it after termination — an empty placeholder.** That's unacceptable; the plan's solution MUST make the tab actually disappear, independent of the user's `closeOnExit` profile setting. The wt.exe server (which hosts ALL tabs in the window) MUST survive untouched.

## Tab-closure acceptance criterion

**The wt tab must visually disappear after hard-terminate, not persist as a 'process exited' placeholder.** Killing the child process alone is not sufficient — empirical evidence shows tabs linger. The plan MUST design a deterministic close-the-tab mechanism. Candidate strategies (plan picks one + justifies):

   T1. **Explicit `wt.exe close-tab` call after kill.** `wt --window <wid> close-tab --tabid <tid>` (verify exact subcommand against Windows Terminal CLI docs). Requires capturing the wt window ID + tab ID at spawn time. Currently NOT in the manifest — needs to be added.
   T2. **Spawn into a dedicated 'crews-member' profile with `closeOnExit: graceful` baked in.** Modify user's wt settings.json at install time. Intrusive but works for all exits. 
   T3. **UI automation (Ctrl+Shift+W keystroke to the focused tab).** Hacky, fragile, last resort.
   T4. **Hybrid T1 + T2.** Most robust, most code.

   Operator leaning: **T1** if wt CLI supports tab-id-targeted close in the user's wt version; fall back to T4 if not. Plan must verify wt CLI capabilities empirically.

## CRITICAL CONSTRAINT — do NOT kill the wt.exe server

The wt.exe server is a long-running process that hosts ALL tabs in a Windows Terminal window. The bookkeeper-lead's own tab, any other crews members' tabs, the operator's dev shells — all share the same wt.exe server. **Killing wt.exe = closing every tab = catastrophic.**

The correct target is the per-tab child process tree:
- The launcher PowerShell script (PID in `manifest.launcherPid`) — may already be exited by the time we want to kill, since its job is to invoke `wt.exe new-tab '<command>'` and exit.
- The Copilot CLI process inside the spawned tab (NOT currently tracked in the manifest — would need to capture at spawn time, possibly via a post-spawn `Get-WmiObject Win32_Process | where CommandLine -match "--name <member-name>"` lookup since Copilot CLI is launched as a grand-child of the wt.exe server, not of our launcher).
- The PowerShell that hosts the Copilot CLI process inside the tab (Copilot CLI runs inside `pwsh` or `powershell` by default in a wt tab).

The plan must:
1. Capture per-member child process PIDs at spawn time (or shortly after) so we know what to kill later.
2. Define a kill strategy that targets ONLY those PIDs — never the wt.exe server PID.
3. Verify the wt.exe `closeOnExit` profile setting is `graceful` (the default) so the tab auto-closes when its child exits.
4. Add a regression test that asserts the wt.exe server PID SURVIVES a hard-terminate (spawn member, capture wt.exe server PID via parent-of-tab-process lookup, hard-terminate the member, assert wt.exe server PID is still alive).

## Design questions for the plan

### Q1. API shape — three reasonable options:

   A. **New `kill-member` subcommand.** Keeps `stop-member` semantics intact for back-compat. `kill-member <name> --crew <crew> [--reason <text>]` does the hard-terminate. Pro: clear semantic separation. Con: two commands for very similar intent.

   B. **`--hard` flag on existing `stop-member`.** Default = soft (current behavior). `stop-member <name> --crew <crew> --hard [--reason <text>]` does hard-terminate. Pro: discoverable. Con: easy to forget the flag and pay the round-trip cost; current bookkeeper habit is to default-call stop-member.

   C. **Flip the default + add `--soft` opt-in.** Default = hard-terminate. `stop-member <name> --crew <crew> [--soft] [--reason <text>]`. Pro: matches operator intent (hard is the common case). Con: breaking change for any consumer that depends on the ack-flow (does anyone?). Plan must investigate.

Plan should pick one and justify. Operator leaning: **C** (flip the default), with a brief deprecation window if there are real consumers of the soft flow.

### Q2. Hard-terminate mechanism — Windows specifics (tab-only, NOT wt.exe server)

Investigate (verify via experimentation):

   - Does `Stop-Process -Id <launcherPid>` even matter? Probably not — by the time hard-terminate runs, the launcher PowerShell has long since exited (its job was to invoke `wt.exe new-tab '...'` and return).
   - Does the manifest currently capture the Copilot CLI process PID inside the tab? Look at `hooks/actors.js::spawnMember` for any post-spawn PID capture. If NOT, plan must add capture — strategies:
      - Post-spawn `Get-WmiObject Win32_Process | where CommandLine -match "--name <safeName>"` lookup, retried with exponential backoff until Copilot CLI process appears (typically 5-15s after spawn).
      - Stamp a unique env var (e.g. `CREWS_MEMBER_PID_MARKER`) via the launcher's `wt.exe new-tab` command and have the spawned shell capture its own PID into the manifest on first turn.
      - Use `COPILOT_LOADER_PID` env var (verified present in this session) — but that's set INSIDE the Copilot CLI process, not accessible from outside.
   - Walk the process-tree parent chain: from the Copilot CLI PID, find its parent (PowerShell inside the tab). Kill PARENT to take down both. STOP walking before reaching the wt.exe server.
   - Use `Stop-Process -Id <pid>` (graceful) first, then `-Force` if process still alive after a timeout.
   - Verify the wt.exe `closeOnExit` setting: read `$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_*\LocalState\settings.json` for the default profile's `closeOnExit` value. If user has set `never`, the tab will linger empty after the child exits; that's a UX nit, not a correctness issue.

   Suggest an exploratory script (deliverable as part of P1 in the plan): spawn a test member with CREWS_NO_LAUNCH=0 (real wt.exe spawn), capture wt.exe server PID + member's launcher PID + Copilot CLI PID via WMI lookup, then try each kill strategy in isolation, observe what survives. The script's output becomes the empirical basis for the kill-strategy decision.

### Q3. Mac / Linux behavior

The current `spawnMember` is Windows-only (errors out on non-Windows with 'spawn-member currently requires Windows'). So Q2's wt.exe-specific design is fine for v1. But the plan should sketch what the equivalent would look like on Mac (Terminal.app via osascript) and Linux (gnome-terminal / xterm via DBus or terminal-emulator CLI) so the API shape doesn't paint us into a corner.

### Q4. Manifest state + audit log

What does the manifest look like after a hard-terminate?

   - `listenerState`: 'exited' (same as soft stop)
   - `actorState`: 'cleared'? Or keep 'active' until a separate `clear-member` runs? Operator's intent — hard-terminate means 'this member is GONE' — so 'cleared' makes sense.
   - `shutdownRequested`: true (signals 'lead authorized this')
   - New `terminatedAt` + `terminationKind: 'hard'` + `terminationReason: <reason>` fields for audit
   - New `terminatedPids: { launcher, copilotCli, hostShell }` for forensic record of what was killed and what survived (esp. wt.exe server PID)
   - Log entry in the manifest's audit history (if such exists)

If actorState flips to 'cleared' automatically on hard-terminate, then `clear-member` becomes redundant for hard-terminated members — the cleanup happens in one shot. The plan should consider whether to merge `kill-member` and `clear-member` into one command, or keep them separate (clear-member also archives mailbox-history; that's a different operation).

### Q5. Edge cases

   - Launcher PID already dead (expected — launcher exits after invoking wt.exe new-tab): no-op for the kill; still target the Copilot CLI child + update manifest state.
   - wt.exe tab already closed by operator (Ctrl+W or X): the Copilot CLI child is already gone; lookup returns no PID; treat as no-op + update manifest.
   - Copilot CLI process not yet discoverable (just-spawned member): retry the WMI lookup with backoff up to N seconds; if still not found, log + soft-fail (proceed with manifest update without actually killing — the process will exit on its own eventually).
   - Multiple PIDs under the same launcher (Copilot CLI may have forked its own children — e.g., Node language servers, child processes for shell tools): walk the process tree DOWN from Copilot CLI's PID and kill all descendants, but STOP at the boundary going UP (never include wt.exe server in the kill set).
   - Member has unreviewed outgoing mail (kind=done not yet consumed by lead): kill anyway. The lead can still read the outbox after the process is gone (outbox is on disk).
   - Member is currently mid-turn (active model invocation): kill anyway. Risk: leaves the model's response truncated, possibly mid-tool-call. Probably acceptable but plan should note the risk.
   - Multiple wt.exe SERVERS running (rare — happens if user has Windows Terminal Stable + Preview both installed). Plan: find the server that owns OUR tab by walking up from Copilot CLI PID; never target any wt.exe server even if multiple are present.

### Q6. AGENTS.md operating-manual update

The codexu AGENTS.md workflow diagram says:

```
lead: /crews:stop-member <name> (do NOT chain into the next phase)
```

If Q1 picks option C (flip default), this stays correct but its semantics change — the bookkeeper should know the new default is hard. If Q1 picks A or B, update the diagram to use the new command/flag. Either way, AGENTS.md needs a line clarifying 'stop-member is now hard by default' or pointing to the new command, AND a safety note: 'hard-terminate kills only the per-tab child process tree; the wt.exe server (and all other tabs) survive untouched.'

## Plan-level guidance

- This is a small-surface change but with non-trivial Windows-process-tree investigation. Allocate a story for the investigation/experimentation specifically.
- Tests: process-kill tests are hard to write portably. Suggest a `tests/stop-member-hard-terminate.test.js` that spawns a no-launch member (CREWS_NO_LAUNCH=1 skips wt.exe), simulates a child process via a sleep, kills it via the new code path, asserts manifest state + process death. Cross-platform skip if not Windows. ALSO a `tests/stop-member-hard-terminate-wt-server-survives.test.js` (Windows-only, optional in CI) that does a REAL wt.exe spawn, captures the wt.exe server PID, hard-terminates the member, and asserts the wt.exe server PID is still alive after the kill.
- Version bump: minor (v1.9.0) if API change; patch if pure flag addition.
- CHANGELOG: document the round-trip-cost rationale, the soft-stop deprecation timeline (if applicable), and the EXPLICIT safety guarantee that hard-terminate never touches the wt.exe server.

## Reference

- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/commands/stop-member.js` — current soft-stop implementation.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/stop-member.js` — CLI mirror.

/plan-with-ralph "Move the crews outbox protocol from one-envelope-per-turn to one-row-per-report JSONL, with terminal-gated batch delivery to the lead.

## Why

Empirically observed 2026-05-29 during smoke-test of impl-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree: a Copilot member emitted multiple <|report kind=\"...\"|> tags in a single Stop-hook turn (3 progress emits followed by a final done emit). The current parseTurnTags (D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/mailbox.js:761) uses first-tag-wins semantics — it locks kind/summary/replyTo to the FIRST tag seen and ignores all subsequent tags. Result: the envelope was written with kind=\"progress\" and the FIRST progress summary, silently discarding the terminal kind=\"done\" with the actual ship report (commit SHAs, validation results, recommendations).

Several attribute-merging fixes were considered (last-wins, terminal-preference, severity-ordered, body-merge variants) but all introduce different edge cases. Operator picked a more invasive but cleaner shape: every <|report|> tag becomes its own outbox row, and consumption batches the trail when at least one terminal row is present.

## Locked design (do NOT re-litigate — plan around these)

### D1. Outbox format

Each <|report ...|> tag in a turn writes ONE row to the member's outbox JSONL. One turn → N rows. Each row carries its own seq, id, writtenAt, kind, summary, body, replyTo, decisions, acks. The legacy 'one envelope per turn' wrapper is retired; consumers operate on rows directly.

### D2. Body partitioning

Each row's body = the prose IMMEDIATELY ABOVE that tag — between this tag and the previous tag in the same turn (or turn start if first). The full-turn message is reconstructable by concatenation but not stored as a separate field. Each row reads as a discrete checkpoint.

### D3. Delivery rule

Lead's listener watches member outboxes. Fires only when the unread tail contains ≥1 terminal-kind row (done/question/blocked). When it fires, delivers ALL unread rows up through the latest as one /crews:review-mail batch. If unread contains only progress rows, listener does NOT fire — keeps waiting.

### D4. Progress-only members

STRICT mode: a member that only ever emits kind=progress and never reaches a terminal never triggers delivery. The lead's mailbox stays empty for that member indefinitely. Operator-acceptable; the manifest's lastKind/lastSummary still update so /list-members shows current activity. If the lead needs to peek at a progress-only trail on demand, they can run /crews:read-member <name> --all.

### D5. Mail-resolution attributes (replyTo / acks / decisions)

Per-row. Each row carries its own replyTo/acks/decisions. The lead's reviewed-cursor advances across the whole delivered batch and credits any row in the batch that resolved an incoming message (matches today's findCurrentDecision semantics, just iterated over multiple rows).

### D6. Body-canonical hard-block

Applied per terminal row (unchanged semantics, just multi-row). If a terminal row has summary > limit AND body < floor, that row is rejected at Stop-hook time. Progress rows exempt as today. A turn with multiple terminal rows where ANY one fails body-canonical → the turn fails; member must re-emit.

## Surface inventory (rough — plan should refine)

- hooks/stop.js — emit per-tag rows; per-row body-canonical detection on terminal rows
- hooks/listener-loop.js + lib/listener-loop.js — terminal-gated batch fire (today fires on any new row)
- hooks/commands/review-mail.js — return multi-row batches in entries[]; cursor semantics across multi-row delivery
- hooks/commands/read-member.js — multi-row return; back-compat with --peek / --since / --all
- hooks/commands/peek-mailbox.js — preview semantics (earliest unread row? earliest unread terminal-batch? plan picks)
- hooks/protocol/report-tags.js — schema for per-row reports; body field becomes required per-row
- hooks/protocol/envelope.js — schema for outbox-row vs the legacy envelope wrapper (retire wrapper)
- hooks/format-progress-tail.js — likely retire; the batch IS the progress tail + the terminal
- hooks/protocol/review-gate.js, force-response logic — verify all mail-resolution checks operate over per-row batches
- tools/*.js — CLI mirrors for review-mail, read-member, peek-mailbox

## Stories suggestion (plan-with-ralph will refine)

- US-001: parseTurnTags extracts per-tag blocks (parser-only change; no on-disk format change yet so the rest of the system is untouched)
- US-002: Stop-hook writes per-tag rows to outbox; outbox-row schema; manifest lastSeq stays roll-forward
- US-003: Listener-loop terminal-gated batch fire
- US-004: review-mail / read-member / peek-mailbox multi-row delivery semantics + cursor advancement
- US-005: Body-canonical per-row; mail-resolution per-row
- US-006: format-progress-tail retirement; progressTail field removal from envelope shape
- US-007: Test sweep — every existing test that asserts one-envelope-per-turn behavior is updated; ~30+ test files reference single-envelope assumptions
- US-008: AGENTS.md (codexu crews-plugin invariants section), README, docs/protocol.md, CHANGELOG (v2.0.0)

Serial within each story; US-001..US-003 must land in order (each builds on the previous). US-004..US-006 can land in parallel after US-003. US-007 + US-008 wrap.

## Tests that MUST exist (current test suite has zero multi-tag coverage — that is why this bug survived)

Regression: the exact failure case observed 2026-05-29.
- Multi-tag turn (progress, progress, done) → outbox has 3 rows. Row 3 is kind=done with the done tag's summary. Row 2 is kind=progress with the second progress tag's summary. Row 1 is kind=progress with the first progress tag's summary. All three rows have distinct body slices (per-tag prose).

Plus:
- Single-tag turn (existing happy path): one row written.
- Terminal-gated delivery: outbox with only progress rows → listener does NOT fire. Append a terminal row → listener fires once, delivers all rows as a batch.
- Multiple terminal rows in one turn (rare but legal): listener delivers the batch through the LATEST terminal; cursor advances past all of them.
- Per-row replyTo: row 1 replies to msg-A, row 2 (terminal) replies to msg-B. Both credited; both incoming messages marked resolved.
- Body-canonical per-row: terminal row with overfull summary + underfull body → that row rejected; progress rows in same turn exempt.

Observed 2026-05-30 with impl-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree: a Copilot member emitted 3 progress tags followed by 1 done tag in a single Stop-hook turn. Current parseTurnTags uses === null guards on kind/summary/replyTo (mailbox.js:761-767), so it locked onto the FIRST progress tag and silently discarded the done tag. ## Locked design (operator picked 2026-05-30)

### D1. Terminal-preference, last-wins-among-terminals

Scan all <|report ...|> tags in the buffer. Pick the canonical tag by:
  1. Scan RIGHT-TO-LEFT, pick the FIRST tag whose kind ∈ {done, question, blocked}
  2. If no terminal tags exist, scan right-to-left for the FIRST tag whose kind === 'progress'
  3. If still no valid kind tag, leave kind=null (existing 'missing kind tag' Stop-hook block fires unchanged)

### D2. Atomic per-tag attributes

The chosen tag's kind, summary, replyTo are taken ATOMICALLY from THAT tag's block — no cross-tag attribute borrowing. A done tag with no summary stays summary=null even if an earlier progress had summary=\"...\".

This is explicitly NOT last-tag-wins (which would pick a stray trailing progress over an earlier terminal). NOT severity-ordered (which complicates the picking rule). NOT body-merging from earlier tags (that comes with v2.0.0 per-row rows).

### D3. ack / decision accumulation

ack/decision attributes continue to accumulate across ALL tags in the buffer (unchanged semantics — acks are about resolving incoming mail, not stating turn intent). Today's lines 768-778 in mailbox.js already iterate. Keep as-is.

### D4. Earlier-tag content is DISCARDED

Earlier progress tags' summaries do not appear in the envelope (no concatenation, no summaryHistory[]). The operator explicitly acknowledged this is acceptable for a stopgap; v2.0.0 preserves them as per-row outbox rows. Document this in the CHANGELOG.

### D5. Version bump

v1.9.3 (patch) — pure bug fix, no API change, no consumer-visible shape change (envelope still has scalar kind/summary/replyTo; just sourced from a different tag now).

/plan-with-ralph "When a crew lead is assigned to an existing terminal session (via /crews-assign-role lead --crew <X> --name <Y>, or on first /crews-status if the role is auto-detected), rename the host wt.exe tab to:

    ♔ <name> (<crew>)

Mirroring the existing member-side convention (members get ♙ <name> (<crew>) stamped at wt.exe spawn time via --title, plus copilot --name + COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 to keep it from being clobbered).

## Background / why

Today members are immediately identifiable by their tab title (♙ <name> (<crew>)) — operator can glance at the wt.exe window and see every crew member at a glance. The lead/orchestrator tab is whatever the operator launched (often just 'PowerShell' or the engine's per-intent OSC titles), making it hard to spot the orchestrating tab in a multi-tab Windows Terminal window. Naming the lead ♔ <name> (<crew>) closes that gap and creates a visually-coherent crew lineup (king + pawns).

## Glyph choice

♔ (white king, U+2654) for lead. Pairs thematically with ♙ (white pawn, U+2659) used for members today. Both are widely-rendered in Windows Terminal default fonts.

Future open question (NOT for this plan): if/when we add other crew roles (advisor, observer, etc.), what chess-piece glyphs map to them? Out of scope for v1.

## Existing member-side machinery (reference)

- D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/actors.js:1781 — sessionDisplayName template for new tabs (♙ <name> (<crew>))
- actors.js:1950 — tabTitle stamped via wt.exe --title at spawn
- actors.js:1822-1826 — comment chain on COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 keeping the title stable for the tab lifetime
- tests/engine-field.test.js, copilot-review-fixes.test.js — existing test coverage

## Surface for THIS task (where lead-side rename happens)

- D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/commands/assign-role.js — likely entry point; emit rename when role transitions to 'lead'
- (Possibly) hooks/session-start.js or equivalent — emit rename on session start if role is already 'lead' from prior manifest

## Mechanism options (planner should pick one with rationale)

### Option A: OSC escape sequence at assign-time

When assign-role transitions to lead, print to stdout:

    \x1b]0;♔ <name> (<crew>)\x07

(or the equivalent \x1b]2;...\x1b\\ ST-terminated form). Lightweight, no shelling out, works on any wt-compatible terminal.

Risk: Copilot's per-intent OSC title updates (controlled by COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE) may clobber the title we set, the same way they did for members until v1.8.12 added the env-var workaround. But we can't stamp COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE on an already-running copilot — that's a startup env-var. So Option A alone may flicker.

### Option B: wt.exe rename-tab subcommand

Shell out to:

    wt.exe --window <current> rename-tab "♔ <name> (<crew>)"

This persists better because wt.exe owns the tab title at the OS level (overrides per-process OSC writes from inside the pane). Downside: requires identifying the current wt window-id (use --window 0 to target the active one), and the tab-rename API may not be available on older wt.exe versions.

### Option C: Both A and B

Emit OSC first (immediate update), then call wt-rename as a follow-up to lock it in. Belt-and-suspenders; small overhead.

### Option D: Just document the limitation; don't auto-rename

Punt. Operator manually renames their tab. (Rejected by operator-requested task scope, but plan should note this as the no-fix baseline.)

Recommended: planner picks A, B, or C with empirical testing on this dev box's Copilot setup. C is likely most-robust.

- Title persists through subsequent Copilot tool calls (does not flicker back to per-intent titles)

- Operator launches Copilot in a non-wt.exe terminal (PowerShell ISE, ConEmu, raw conhost). OSC may still work; wt-rename will silently fail. Plan should not crash in those cases.
- Lead session is started via /crews-resume-crew or auto-detected from prior manifest on SessionStart — title should still be set then, not only on the assign-role command.
- Operator renames the tab manually after assign — do we re-clobber on next heartbeat, or respect operator intent? Plan should pick a policy (likely: only emit on role transitions, not on every heartbeat).

## Out of scope

- Cross-platform (mac/Linux iTerm/gnome-terminal title sequences). Windows-only as members are.

## Background

Observed 2026-05-29 across three plan-spawn cycles (codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement, crews-stop-member-hard-terminate-no-envelope x2, ralph-overview-data-relocation-and-json-migration) that /plan-with-ralph does NOT manage its own worktree. Each plan member had to be instructed via the bookkeeper-lead's spawn-prompt to create a worktree manually, e.g.:

```
WORKTREE MANDATE: use `git worktree add ../codexu-plan-<slug> -b ralph/plan-<task-id> main` and do ALL work inside that worktree.
```

That's bookkeeper-side toil per spawn AND a source of bugs:
- Three sibling-of-repo worktrees were created in error (`../codexu-plan-wrapper-retirement`, `../codexu-plan-hard-terminate`, `../codexu-plan-hard-terminate-v2`) because the lead's spawn-prompt followed an outdated AGENTS.md pattern.
- One leftover worktree ended up at `D:/codexu-plan-data-relocation` (root of D: drive) — definitely not where any documented convention says.

Meanwhile /implement-with-ralph DOES auto-manage a worktree at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/` (verified from existing worktrees on codexu). The asymmetry is the bug.

## Goal

When /plan-with-ralph is invoked, the skill itself should:
1. Determine task-id from the invocation (already in scope via the spawn prompt or --from-brainstorm path).
2. Create a worktree at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/plan/` on a fresh topic branch `ralph/plan-<task-id>` (or `-v2`, `-v3` suffix if siblings already exist on origin — investigate edge case).
3. Do all plan work INSIDE that worktree (commit deliverables there, push the topic branch, etc.).
4. Report the worktree path + topic branch in its final kind=done message so the lead knows where to FF from and what to clean up.
5. NOT touch the lead's primary working dir (which stays on main per AGENTS.md).

## Design questions for the plan

### Q1. Worktree path: subdir or no?

   A. `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/` (matches /implement-with-ralph's existing layout exactly)
   B. `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/plan/` (with a `plan/` subdir, so if both plan + impl are open at the same time they don't conflict)
   C. `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree-plan/` (sibling-of-worktree, different basename)

   Lean toward **B**: subdir lets the plan worktree coexist with a future impl worktree at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/impl/`. Plan should verify whether /implement-with-ralph would conflict with a same-task worktree dir already existing.

### Q2. Topic branch naming and v2/v3 collision

If the lead re-spawns a plan member after the first one shipped (e.g., the v2 case observed 2026-05-29 where the plan was corrected based on operator feedback), the topic branch `ralph/plan-<task-id>` already exists on origin. Strategies:

   A. Skill detects the collision and auto-suffixes `-v2`, `-v3`, etc. (what member B did manually for the hard-terminate task)
   B. Skill fails fast and requires the lead to delete the old branch first
   C. Skill always uses a UUID/timestamp suffix

   Lean toward **A** (auto-suffix). Matches what already happened organically in the smoke-test session.

### Q3. Cleanup story

Who cleans up the plan worktree + topic branch after the lead FF's?

   A. Lead does it manually (current state, post-FF cleanup is bookkeeper toil)
   B. Skill provides a 'plan-complete' subcommand the lead can run after FF that nukes both
   C. Skill auto-detects post-FF state on next invocation (e.g., the worktree's branch HEAD is reachable from origin/main → safe to remove)

   Lean toward **B** (explicit subcommand) — cleanest API. The lead's post-FF flow becomes: `git merge --ff-only <sha> && git push origin main && /plan-with-ralph cleanup <task-id>`.

### Q4. Sequencing with the existing /implement-with-ralph skill

/implement-with-ralph uses `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/`. If Q1 picks A (same path for plan and impl), there's a collision if both phases are active. If B (with `plan/` subdir), need to also rename impl's worktree to `impl/` subdir for symmetry — that's a breaking change for /implement-with-ralph. Plan should think about whether to:

   - Migrate both skills together (synchronized rename)
   - Keep /implement-with-ralph at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/` and put /plan-with-ralph at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree-plan/` to avoid the symmetry burden
   - Some other naming scheme

## Reference

- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/skills/plan-with-ralph/SKILL.md` (or wherever the plan-with-ralph skill body lives) — current behavior, no worktree auto-management.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` — reference for how the impl skill manages its worktree (the design to mirror).
- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/AGENTS.md` 'Branch + worktree discipline' section — codified worktree-placement convention (2026-05-29 update); this task's deliverable should match.
- Smoke-test session 2026-05-29: three plan-member spawns that each needed manual worktree mandates in the spawn prompt; one cleanup miss at `D:/codexu-plan-data-relocation`.

## Phase discipline + reporting

This is the PLAN phase. Produce ONLY a plan deliverable. Do NOT chain into impl.

COMMIT TARGET: lead is on `main`. Create a worktree at `.ralph/jobs/ralph-orchestration-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree/worktree/plan/` (eating our own dog food — use the convention this task is establishing). Commit on `ralph/plan-ralph-orchestration-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree`, push to `origin`, report commit SHA + branch + worktree path in kind=done body.

REPORTING (crews v1.8.x body-canonical hard-block): final turn ends with `<|report kind=\"done\" summary=\"<short>\"|>`. Substantive content (commit SHA, branch, worktree path, picked options Q1-Q4, open questions, anomalies) in PROSE BODY. DO NOT add `reply-to=\"spawn\"`."
