actions.label: Brainstorm
actions.prompt:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Push cross-engine plugin-path resolution UPSTREAM into the ralph-overview plugin's overview-init skill so every consumer gets a working pnpm sync-ralph-state + pnpm overview under BOTH Claude Code AND Copilot CLI, without each consumer hand-rolling a per-repo resolver wrapper.

## Why this matters

The ralph-overview plugin's current `scripts/init-consumer.mjs` (./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/init-consumer.mjs lines 10-15) emits PACKAGE_SCRIPTS of the form `node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs <sub> --repo .`. Those scripts break on Copilot CLI because Copilot exports NO equivalent env var (verified 2026-05-29 against https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference — Copilot exposes only COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID, COPILOT_CLI, COPILOT_CLI_BINARY_VERSION, COPILOT_LOADER_PID, COPILOT_RUN_APP, COPILOT_HOME).

Codexu worked around this with a hand-rolled `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` wrapper that probes both engine install paths. That wrapper has now been committed (task `codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement`, plan @ commit `e527f83e`, impl shipped 2026-05-29) as a SHORT-TERM fix — but every NEW consumer of the plugin would have to author the same wrapper themselves. The long-term fix is to push the resolution UPSTREAM into the plugin.

Reference: codexu's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (now tracked in the codexu repo) is the working reference implementation of the cascade — it's ~130 LoC, self-contained, and has been battle-tested 2026-05-29 against Copilot CLI install + env-override + local-dev fallback (see `.ralph/jobs/codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement/smoke-test.md`). The plugin-side version would be ~identical but unit-tested.

## Design axes to pressure-test

### Axis 1 — Where does the wrapper live in the consumer repo?

A. **`bin/ralph-overview.mjs` in the consumer repo** (matches codexu's current pattern). Pro: simple, discoverable, matches what package.json scripts already say. Con: consumer repo now ships a generated file that's tracked in git; regenerating on plugin upgrade requires explicit `overview-init --force` step.
B. **`scripts/ralph-overview.mjs`** instead of `bin/`. Same trade-offs but avoids any `/bin/` gitignore-by-convention concerns (codexu had to un-ignore `/bin/` to make this work; other consumers may have similar global gitignore rules).
C. **Inline in `package.json` scripts** via `node -e "...resolver code..." <sub>`. Pro: zero tracked files. Con: cross-shell quoting hell on Windows + cmd + PowerShell + bash; long inline strings are unreadable and hard to debug.
D. **Install into `node_modules/.bin/ralph-overview`** as a postinstall step. Pro: matches npm/pnpm convention. Con: requires the plugin to ship as an npm package or have a postinstall hook that pnpm runs reliably across both engine installs.

Lean toward **A** (matches codexu's existing layout, minimal surprise). But brainstorm should weigh B vs A for new consumers without legacy.

### Axis 2 — Cross-engine install-path cascade

The wrapper must probe (at least) these install layouts:
1. `$RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` env override (escape hatch for plugin-dev)
2. `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/<plugin>/` (Claude Code harness-set)
3. `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<latest>/` (Claude Code cache)
4. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<latest>/` (Claude Code user install)
5. `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/` (Copilot CLI user install, no per-version subdir)
6. Local-dev fallback? (codexu has one at `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/` — should the plugin-emitted wrapper include any local-dev escape, or rely on RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT for plugin-author iteration?)

Brainstorm should decide on the canonical cascade order + whether to expose any plugin-side configuration of additional probe paths.

### Axis 3 — `overview-init` API for the new emit

Current `initConsumer({addPackageJsonScripts: true})` writes scripts only. New shape options:

A. **Additive flag:** `addPackageJsonScripts: true, addConsumerWrapper: true` (default both true).
B. **Single flag rename:** rename to `addPackageJsonScriptsAndWrapper: true` to signal the new bundled emission.
C. **Subcommand split:** `overview-init` is now always-bundled; add `overview-init --wrapper-only` and `overview-init --scripts-only` for advanced cases.

Lean toward **A** (additive flag, both default true). Existing consumers calling `addPackageJsonScripts: true` should opt in to `addConsumerWrapper: true` explicitly the first time, to avoid surprise file creation.

### Axis 4 — Migration story for codexu (the current consumer with a hand-committed wrapper)

Codexu's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` is now tracked. When this plugin task ships v2.5.0+ with the auto-emit feature, codexu can:

A. Re-run `overview-init --force` to replace its hand-committed wrapper with the plugin-emitted one (and stay in sync with future plugin upgrades automatically).
B. Keep its hand-committed wrapper indefinitely; never opt into the auto-emit feature.
C. Run `overview-init --diff` first to see what would change, then decide.

Plan should document the recommended migration path for codexu + any other consumers that may exist by then.

### Axis 5 — Test coverage of every install layout

The plugin-side wrapper SHOULD ship with unit tests that simulate each install layout. The codexu hand-rolled wrapper has zero tests today — this is one of the long-term wins of pushing it upstream. Test cases at minimum:

- `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` set to a valid path → resolves to it
- `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` set to an invalid path → warns + falls through
- `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set with direct subdir → resolves to it
- `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set with cache versioned subdirs → picks latest by lexical sort
- `~/.claude/plugins/cache/...` versioned subdirs → picks latest
- `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/...` single dir → resolves to it
- All cascade misses → exits 2 with the friendly install-instruction message
- Found install missing the dispatcher file → exits 3
- `--repo` arg present → preserved; absent → defaulted to `gitRepoRoot()`

### Axis 6 — Out of scope for this brainstorm (separate concerns)

- The Copilot CLI plugin-install dependency-installation gap (the 2026-05-29 smoke test found `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/.../ralph-overview/` lacks `node_modules/`). That's a Copilot CLI / plugin-publish-pipeline issue, NOT something the wrapper can fix — the wrapper successfully dispatches to the install path; it's the install that's incomplete. Surface as a separate plugin-author followup if not already tracked.
- Option D from the codexu-side plan (Copilot CLI feature request for per-plugin env-var parity with `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`). Out of band; pursued via GitHub issue.

## Deliverable

At end of brainstorm Phase 5, produce `.ralph/brainstorms/ralph-overview-init-consumer-cross-engine-wrapper/selected-direction.md` with:

- Recommended wrapper location (A/B/C/D from Axis 1).
- Final cascade order + whether to support plugin-side configurable additional probe paths.
- Recommended `overview-init` API shape (A/B/C from Axis 3).
- Recommended codexu migration path (Axis 4).
- Test plan outline (Axis 5).
- Plugin version bump target (v2.5.0 minor candidate, or other).
- Open questions for the planner.

Do NOT chain into /plan-with-ralph. The bookkeeper spawns a fresh plan-ralph-overview-init-consumer-cross-engine-wrapper member from the selected-direction.md per phase discipline.

## Reference

- `.ralph/jobs/codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement/plan.md` (commit `e527f83e`) — the parent plan that recommended this task as Option C1.
- `.ralph/jobs/codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement/smoke-test.md` — empirical evidence the codexu wrapper works under Copilot CLI.
- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (committed during impl of the parent task) — the working reference implementation to port upstream.
- `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/init-consumer.mjs` — the plugin file to modify; current PACKAGE_SCRIPTS constant at lines 10-15.
- `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs` — the plugin's own bin dispatcher (self-locating; reference for what env vars the plugin's runtime expects)."

Observed 2026-05-27 in the overview-bookkeeper session: when the Stop hook forces a synchronous review-mail (because lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq), the cursor advances and the unreviewed-mail gate clears. If the agent then ends its turn with a text-only response (no further tool calls), the Stop hook accepts the turn-end and the listener is NOT re-armed. The next inbound message arrives with no watcher attached. The PreToolUse hook only re-arms when the agent attempts a tool call, so the gap persists until the agent acts on its own initiative.

This is symmetric to the bug the crews-review-mid-turn-v160 task was fixing (mid-turn review-required not enforced) but on the Stop side: 'turn-end without armed listener' should be blocked, just like 'turn-end with unreviewed mail' is blocked today.

## Fix

In `plugins/crews/hooks/stop.js`:

1. Read the actor's manifest.json `listenerState` field (canonical source — same field the PreToolUse hook reads).
2. If `listenerState !== 'armed'` (i.e. 'exited', 'unknown', missing, or stale per heartbeat), emit the same exit-code-2 blocking-error pattern used elsewhere:

   ```
   ReviewRequiredError: turn-end without armed listener for name \"<name>\" (crew=\"<crew>\").
   
   Run this Bash tool call now:
     command: node '<plugin>/tools/crews.js' arm --name <name> --crew <crew> --cwd <cwd> --session-id <session-id>
     run_in_background: true
   ```

3. Honor the existing v1.6.0 progress-envelope exemption — Stop hook should NOT block when the actor has only emitted a `kind=progress` envelope and there's no inbound mail expected (otherwise every progress-only turn would forever require a listener). The check should fire when:
   - The actor's role is `lead` OR `member` (any active actor).
   - The kind tag is one of `done`, `question`, `blocked` (terminal-ish kinds expect a sender response).

/plan-with-ralph "Fix the codex-exec.mjs spawn-without-shell bug in ai-developer-toolkit's ralph-orchestration plugin.

## Problem

`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/codex-exec.mjs` at v5.45.0 invokes:

```js
spawn('codex', args, { stdio: 'inherit', cwd, env })
```

Missing `shell: true`. On Windows with the Node.js CVE-2024-27980 patch (Node 18.20.5+, 20.18.1+, 22.11.0+), bare-name commands without shell context fail with ENOENT. The result: every codex iteration (and every review-changes Codex reviewer subagent) on Windows dies in ~800ms. v5.44.0 (the prior version) used a bash wrapper `codex-exec.sh` that called codex via Git Bash, so the issue didn't exist.

## Workaround in place

The impl-overview-data-dynamic-stages-schema member (running 2026-05-27) discovered the bug mid-flight. Workaround applied:

1. **Env var fallback:** Set `CODEX_EXEC_SCRIPT=C:/Users/evmitran/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-orchestration/5.44.0/codex-exec.sh` — the `resolveEngineScript` helper in v5.45 honors this and routes to the v5.44 bash wrapper.
2. **In-place patch:** Edited the cached v5.45.0 `src/codex-exec.mjs` to add `shell: true` to the spawn call, so review-changes subagents (which spawn their own ralph-orchestration instances) also work.

Auto-memory: `feedback_codex_exec_v545_windows_spawn` documents both.

## Fix

In `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/codex-exec.mjs`:

```diff
- spawn('codex', args, { stdio: 'inherit', cwd, env })
+ spawn('codex', args, { stdio: 'inherit', cwd, env, shell: true })
```

Also audit `src/copilot-exec.mjs` and any other bare-name `spawn` calls in the Node port for the same bug. Likely applies to `codex-reviewer.mjs`, `copilot-reviewer.mjs`, etc. — anywhere v5.45 ported from a shell script to Node.

Secondary consideration: `shell: true` opens command-injection risk if any argv element is attacker-controlled. Audit how `args` is constructed. For our use case args come from prompt strings written by the orchestrator — operator-trusted — so `shell: true` is acceptable. But document the threat model explicitly in a comment near the spawn call to prevent future regressions from introducing untrusted args.

Alternative implementation: use `execFile` with the absolute path to codex (`spawnSync('where', ['codex']).stdout` resolved once at startup), avoiding shell entirely. More work but safer. Plan should evaluate both and recommend.

1. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/codex-exec.mjs` — the fix (shell: true OR execFile-with-resolved-path).

4. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/CHANGELOG.md` — entry for v5.45.1 (or v5.46) with the Windows-spawn-fix note.
5. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/package.json` — version bump.
6. Add a unit test (if the plugin has a test suite) that mocks spawn + asserts `shell: true` is set on Windows. If no test suite, skip.

## Acceptance

- Fix applied to all affected spawn calls in ralph-orchestration v5.45.x → v5.45.1 (or v5.46.0 if version bump policy is minor-on-fix).
- A clean install of the new version on this Windows host successfully spawns codex without the CODEX_EXEC_SCRIPT workaround.
- After fix lands and is installed, removing the workaround memory `feedback_codex_exec_v545_windows_spawn` is the lead's housekeeping job.
- Existing cross-platform behavior unchanged (Mac/Linux still work).
- Pushed to BOTH ai-developer-toolkit remotes (Evyatar108 + gim-home).

## Problem

Observed 2026-05-28 during 3 concurrent plan-member spawns in the overview-bookkeeper crew: plan-crews-envelope-body-canonical-for-all-kinds and plan-crews-lead-suppress-kind-tag both happened to spawn within the same wall-clock second and write to overlapping staging paths. The later member overwrote the earlier one's feature-request.txt mid-Phase-2, causing the earlier's Codex+Copilot research to receive corrupt content. The earlier member recovered by switching to a uniquely-suffixed path, but the recovery wasn't free.

## Root cause

The staging path is computed as <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<session_id>/ where session_id is a bare timestamp slug at second-granularity. Two members spawning within the same second produce the same slug.

## Fix options

(a) Append member-name (kebab-case) to the slug: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp>-<member-name>/
(b) Append PID: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp>-<pid>/
(c) Append nanosecond timestamp: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp-ns>/
(d) Add random suffix: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp>-<random4>/

/plan-with-ralph "Codify and enforce the crews protocol contract that the prose body carries canonical content for all review-surfacing kind tags (done, question, blocked, possibly progress) — not the summary attribute.

## Why

Observed 2026-05-28 in overview-bookkeeper coordination: a member (impl-ralph-overview-watcher-consumer-workspace-root) emitted kind=question with a 600-char summary attribute carrying the full question content + body = 'Adding the ack for the prior operator authorization message' (a 55-char ack stub). The bookkeeper lead received only the ack stub in review-mail because:

1. The summary attribute should have been ≤120 chars per SessionStart briefing.
2. The substantive content belongs in the prose body, not the summary attribute.
3. The summary-drop bug (separately tracked at crews-review-mail-summary-payload-fallback) compounded the impact, but even without that bug, the audit trail in mailbox-history.jsonl would have only had the ack stub as the searchable / human-readable record of what the member was actually asking.

The operator's directive: ALL kind values that propagate to the lead's review queue (done, question, blocked, and arguably progress) should carry the substantive content in the body, mirroring the existing kind=done convention that members already follow. The summary attribute remains a quick-look for the manifest's lastSummary field.

## Design space

### Axis 1 — Documentation

Clarify in:
- SessionStart briefing prose (the long instructions every new session reads at startup) — explicit 'body is canonical for X kinds' line.
- crews/CLAUDE.md operator manual.
- crews/docs/protocol.md if it exists; otherwise add one.
- copilot-plugin mirrors.

### Axis 2 — Enforcement (Stop-hook detection)

When a member emits a kind tag with summary attribute > N chars AND body < M chars, the Stop hook can:

**(a) docs-only** — no Stop-hook change; rely on operator + bookkeeper to flag misuse.
**(b) warn** — Stop hook emits a transcript-visible warning ('your summary attribute is long but your body is short; the audit trail will only have the body. Consider moving the content into the body before the tag.') without blocking the turn. Member sees but may proceed.
**(c) hard block** — Stop hook BLOCKS turn-end with an actionable message. Member must restructure prose before stop succeeds. Symmetric to the v1.6.2 listener-arm gate.
**(d) auto-promote** — when summary > N and body < M, the envelope-writer copies summary to body before persistence. The member's intent is preserved without operator intervention; the protocol mistake is silently corrected.

Thresholds N (summary cap above which we suspect content-stuffing) and M (body floor below which we suspect ack-only). The audit member observed N=600 / M=55 in the reproducer; plausible defaults: N=200, M=50.

### Axis 3 — Which kinds get enforcement?

- All of {done, question, blocked} — these are the review-required kinds.
- progress is more nuanced: idle progress envelopes legitimately have short bodies; enforcement here would create false positives.

Plan should evaluate whether progress envelopes need the same treatment, given the v1.6.0 progress-envelope exemption from review-required.

## Files to touch

1. plugins/crews/hooks/stop.js — if (b), (c), or (d): the kind-tag parser captures summary/body lengths and applies the chosen action.

4. plugins/crews/hooks/SessionStart.js (or wherever the long briefing prose lives) — clarification on the body-canonical rule for {done, question, blocked}.
5. plugins/crews/tests/stop-decision.test.js — fixtures for the (b)/(c)/(d) behavior on long-summary + short-body envelopes.
6. CHANGELOG.md + version bump.

## Operator-facing open questions

1. Which option for axis 2: (a)/(b)/(c)/(d)?
2. Threshold values N + M.
3. Whether progress envelopes are in-scope or exempt.

## Acceptance

- SessionStart briefing prose clearly states 'body is canonical for kind={done, question, blocked}'.
- crews CLAUDE.md documents the rule + the thresholds.
- Stop-hook behavior matches the chosen option from axis 2.
- New tests cover the new behavior (lazy-summary detection, no false-positives on legitimate short-body progress envelopes).
- Existing tests still pass (v1.6.2 listener-arm gate, v1.7.x sessionId pointer, etc).

Version bump: v1.8.0 minor (if (c) or (d) — behavioral change) OR v1.7.4 patch (if (a) or (b) — additive). Multi-remote push. Local-main FF + push-main pattern per operator preference.

Note sequencing: this task can ship before, after, or in parallel with crews-review-mail-summary-payload-fallback (v1.7.3). They address different layers: this is producer-side discipline; that is consumer-side resilience."

/plan-with-ralph "Add a Phase 5.5 retrospective subagent that gathers follow-up task suggestions from a ralph impl run. Sibling to DSAT-analyst + skill-suggester (Phase 5.5 currently spawns those in parallel for post-impl retrospective).

## Motivation

Observed 2026-05-27 in the overview-bookkeeper session: after every impl ship, the bookkeeper manually scans the iteration artifacts for 'are there follow-up tasks worth tracking?' Today the bookkeeper found 3 such tasks from the just-shipped overview-data-dynamic-stages-schema + crews v1.6.2 work: (1) ralph-overview watcher parse-overview-data.mjs two-statement-preamble limitation (Phase 5b F-002 wont_fix); (2) 3 pre-existing Windows test-isolation failures in crews tests (documented in notepad.md but not captured as a task); (3) cross-platform smoke for v5.45.1's shell:true fix (deferred to Mac/Linux verification).

This manual scan is high-leverage but easy to forget. Automating it via a Phase 5.5 retrospective agent ensures every ship surfaces its loose ends.

## Design

### Agent location + naming

- Lives at `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/agents/followup-task-gatherer/SKILL.md` (or wherever DSAT-analyst.md + skill-suggester.md live — match the existing convention).
- Agent name: `followup-task-gatherer` (singular, matches existing kebab-case pattern).
- Tools: read-only agent — Read, Grep, Glob. Does NOT write to disk except its single output artifact.

### Inputs the agent reads

1. `.ralph/jobs/<id>/job-state.json` — phase/story state.
2. `.ralph/jobs/<id>/code-review-findings.json` + `docs-review-findings.json` — focus on `status: wont_fix` and `status: deferred` entries.
3. `.ralph/jobs/<id>/notepad.md` — Open Questions section + Deferred Questions table.
4. `.ralph/jobs/<id>/plan.md` — Open Questions for the planner section.
5. `git diff <base_branch>..HEAD --name-only` — high-level file list of what changed.
6. `git log <base_branch>..HEAD --format='%h %s'` — commit summaries.

### Output artifact

`.ralph/jobs/<id>/followup-suggestions.json` with schema:

```json
{
  "generatedAt": "2026-05-27T...",
  "jobSlug": "...",
  "suggestions": [
    {
      "id": "suggested-task-slug",
      "scope": "ralph-overview | crews | codexu | codex | etc",
      "lifecycle": "tracked",
      "rationale": "1-3 sentence why this is worth tracking",
      "sourceFinding": {
        "type": "wont_fix_finding | deferred_finding | open_question | notepad_entry | observed_gap",
        "reference": "F-002 (Phase 5b docs review) / notepad.md line 47 / plan.md Open Questions #3",
        "excerpt": "verbatim quote of the source"
      },
      "suggestedPrompts": {
        "brainstorm": "...",  // if fuzzy
        "plan": "..."          // if concrete
      },
      "recommendedPhase": "brainstorm | plan",
      "estimatedSize": "S | M | L",
      "dependencies": ["other-task-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Phase 5.5 integration

In `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` (or whatever file currently spawns DSAT + skill-suggester):

- Find the Phase 5.5 step that launches `DSAT-analyst` + `skill-suggester` in parallel.
- Add `followup-task-gatherer` to the same parallel batch (3 agents total, all read-only, all writing their own .json artifact).
- Same retrospective semantics: Phase 5.5 is post-impl, doesn't gate kind=done, doesn't block Phase 6.

### Operator-gated, NOT auto-write

**CRITICAL invariant:** the agent writes to `.ralph/jobs/<id>/followup-suggestions.json` ONLY. It does NOT write to `.ralph-overview/data.json`. The bookkeeper lead reviews the suggestions when shipping and decides which to add. This preserves the 'hand-curated invariant' on .ralph-overview/data.json (per the codexu CLAUDE.md and the upcoming overview-data-ship-manifest task design).

Optional v2: an MCP tool `overview.suggest_followups({jobId})` reads the .json + lets the bookkeeper bulk-add via an operator-confirm flow. Out of scope for v1.

## Files to touch

1. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/agents/followup-task-gatherer/SKILL.md` — new agent (mirror DSAT-analyst structure).
2. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` — Phase 5.5 batch addition.
3. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/schemas/followup-suggestions-schema.json` — JSON schema for the output artifact.
4. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/CHANGELOG.md` + version bump (v5.46.0 — minor since it's an additive feature, no API break).
5. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/package.json` + `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` version bumps.
6. Test fixtures under `tests/` if the plugin has them.

## Acceptance

- AC-1: After Phase 5.5 retrospective on a test impl run, `.ralph/jobs/<id>/followup-suggestions.json` exists and validates against the schema.
- AC-2: When the impl has zero wont_fix/deferred findings AND zero notepad Open Questions, `suggestions[]` is empty (no false positives).
- AC-3: When the impl has a Phase 5b wont_fix finding (sample fixture), `suggestions[]` contains at least one entry with `sourceFinding.type = 'wont_fix_finding'` and `sourceFinding.reference` pointing at the finding ID.
- AC-4: When notepad.md Open Questions section contains an unanswered question, it appears as a suggestion with `sourceFinding.type = 'open_question'`.
- AC-5: DSAT-analyst + skill-suggester continue to run unchanged (regression check).
- AC-6: Phase 5.5 completes within +2 minutes of pre-feature baseline (the third agent runs in parallel; shouldn't extend wall time).
- AC-7: `followup-suggestions.json` is gitignored at the .ralph/jobs/ level OR is intentionally tracked — the plan decides which. Default suggestion: track it (history is useful).

## Workflow

Concrete enough to skip /brainstorm-with-ralph. Run /plan-with-ralph directly. Probably decomposes into 3-4 stories (agent prompt + schema + Phase 5.5 integration + tests).

Version bump: v5.46.0 (minor) — additive retrospective agent, no breaking change. Multi-remote push (Evyatar108 + gim-home)."

/plan-with-ralph "Integrate ai-developer-toolkit as a git submodule of codexu. Today the toolkit lives at ./ai-developer-toolkit as a sibling repo with two remotes (Evyatar108 origin + gim-home work). Codexu references it via absolute paths in spawn-launcher scripts, CLAUDE.md instructions, bookkeeper memory, plan documents, and ad-hoc commands. This is fragile (breaks on a different machine layout) and prevents codexu from version-pinning the toolkit commit it depends on.

## Target structure

```
D:/harness-efforts/codexu/
├── .gitmodules                  # add new submodule entry
├── ai-developer-toolkit/        # NEW submodule (was: ./ai-developer-toolkit/)
│   ├── plugins/
│   │   ├── ralph-overview/
│   │   ├── crews/
│   │   └── ralph-orchestration/
│   └── ...
├── codex/                       # existing submodule (gim-home/codex)
├── plans/
├── tools/
├── packages/
└── ...
```

## Submodule remote URL

Use `https://github.com/gim-home/ai-developer-toolkit.git` per the codex/ submodule precedent (already uses gim-home). The local checkout's `origin` (Evyatar108) becomes a non-default remote that the operator adds manually for the push-to-both convention.

## Migration steps

### Pre-flight

1. **Verify upstream toolkit state.** Confirm both Evyatar108/ai-developer-toolkit and gim-home/ai-developer-toolkit point at the same main HEAD (the last merge commit was `e65e8161` per recent bookkeeping). If they diverge, sync first.
2. **Snapshot the current absolute paths.** Run `grep -rn './ai-developer-toolkit\|D:\\ai-developer-toolkit' D:/harness-efforts/codexu/ --include='*.md' --include='*.js' --include='*.mjs' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ps1' --include='*.json' --include='*.txt'` to enumerate every reference. Save the list.
3. **Check the user .claude/settings.json MCP server registration.** If `mcpServers.ralph-overview` references `./ai-developer-toolkit/` directly (vs the cached plugin location), it'll need update — but verify this is in scope; the published-plugin cache at `C:/Users/evmitran/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/<ver>/` is separate from a dev-mode source reference.

### Submodule add

4. **Add submodule from inside codexu.** 
   ```
   cd D:/harness-efforts/codexu
   git submodule add https://github.com/gim-home/ai-developer-toolkit.git ai-developer-toolkit
   git submodule update --init
   ```
   This creates `./ai-developer-toolkit/` checkout, adds `.gitmodules` entry, and stages a submodule pointer commit at the current main HEAD.

5. **Add Evyatar108 remote to the local submodule checkout.** Without this, the operator can't push to the personal fork.
   ```
   cd ai-developer-toolkit
   git remote add evyatar108 https://github.com/Evyatar108/ai-developer-toolkit.git
   cd ..
   ```

6. **Commit the submodule pointer.** Single commit in codexu: `chore: add ai-developer-toolkit submodule at <SHA>`.

### Path rewrite

7. **Rewrite the absolute paths captured in step 2.** For each file in the snapshot:
   - `./ai-developer-toolkit/...` → `./ai-developer-toolkit/...` (or relative to file location: `../ai-developer-toolkit/...` if needed).
   - Backslash variants: `D:\\ai-developer-toolkit\\...` → forward-slash relative form.
   - Spawn launchers under `.crews/spawn-launchers/*.ps1` contain `Set-Location './ai-developer-toolkit'`-style lines that pin the toolkit absolute path — update to `Set-Location '$PSScriptRoot/../../ai-developer-toolkit'` or equivalent.
   - DO NOT rewrite paths inside `ai-developer-toolkit/` itself (those are the toolkit's own repo content, not codexu's).
   - DO NOT rewrite paths inside cached plugin locations at `C:/Users/evmitran/.claude/plugins/cache/` (those are the published artifact, not source).
   - DO update bookkeeper memory entries at `C:/Users/evmitran/.claude/projects/D--harness-efforts-codexu/memory/*.md` — these are codexu-scoped memories and reference toolkit paths.

8. **Verify each rewrite still works.** Particular care for:
   - `.crews/spawn-launchers/*.ps1` — these are auto-generated by crews plugin spawnMember; check that the next spawn-member call produces a launcher with the relative path.
   - `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/CLAUDE.md` (untracked) — update the bookkeeper operating manual.
   - `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` — update doc references.
   - In-flight task plan.md files under `.ralph/jobs/*/plan.md` — leave as-is (those are in-flight committed state).

### Crew spawn pattern

9. **Spawn-member command in CLAUDE.md.** The current invocation is:
   ```
   node <plugin>/tools/crews.js spawn-member <name> --crew ralph-pipeline --cwd D:/harness-efforts/codexu --state-cwd D:/harness-efforts/codexu --as overview-bookkeeper -- <prompt>
   ```
   The `<plugin>` placeholder is the cached plugin path. With submodule integration, dev-mode (uncached) spawn-member calls could use `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/crews.js`. Update the CLAUDE.md guidance to clarify when to use cached-plugin path vs in-tree submodule path — likely the cached path stays canonical for production use, while the submodule path is for dev-mode editing.

10. **Verify member auto-resolution.** Spawned members rely on `--state-cwd` to find `.crews/`. Confirm members work with the submodule-integrated layout.

### CI invariant

11. **Add invariant check.** A pre-commit hook or CI workflow that checks codexu's CLAUDE.md / docs references to ralph-overview / crews plugin versions match the in-tree submodule version. Prevents drift between 'doc says version X' and 'submodule has version Y'.
   - Specifically: `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/CLAUDE.md` mentions crews v1.6.0, ralph-overview v2.1.0. After submodule integration, the version is whatever's at `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/<plugin>/package.json` or `plugin.json`. CI lints for the version-string match.

### Bookkeeper memory updates

12. **Update bookkeeper auto-memory:**
   - `feedback_cross_repo_impl_worktree_mandate.md` — describes 'sibling repo' cross-repo coordination. With ai-developer-toolkit as a submodule, the 'sibling' framing changes. Update to reflect that ai-developer-toolkit lives INSIDE codexu now, and worktree mandates are scoped accordingly.
   - `feedback_crews_spawn_state_cwd_override.md` — the --state-cwd flag rule. Update example paths.
   - `feedback_plan_member_branch_cherry_pick.md` — if the cherry-pick worktree pattern changes for submodule edits, update.
   - Any memory referencing `./ai-developer-toolkit/...` — sweep + update.

### Acceptance

- `.gitmodules` lists ai-developer-toolkit submodule at `./ai-developer-toolkit/` with gim-home URL.
- `git submodule update --init` brings the toolkit in cleanly.
- Zero `./ai-developer-toolkit` or `D:\\ai-developer-toolkit` references remain in tracked codexu files (excluding .ralph/jobs/*/plan.md historical artifacts and the cached plugin location).
- Crew spawn-member works with the new layout (verify by spawning a test member).
- MCP server registration unchanged (cache path still works) OR updated if dev-mode needs in-tree path.
- Bookkeeper docs (CLAUDE.md, codexu-roadmap.md) describe the submodule integration; spawn-member examples use relative paths or the cached path with a note about the new option.
- 4+ bookkeeper memory entries updated.
- CI invariant check passes (versions match).
- ai-developer-toolkit's own git history is untouched (no commits made inside the submodule as part of this task).

## Sequencing relative to other in-flight work

The 4 overview-data-* tasks (dynamic-stages-schema, ship-manifest, context-scalability, naming-rebrand) all reference ./ai-developer-toolkit paths in their planPrompts. Two options the planner should evaluate:

- **Land submodule FIRST** — then the 4 overview-data-* tasks naturally use relative paths in any new content they write. Path rewrite churn is concentrated in this task.
- **Land submodule LAST** — keep absolute paths stable while the in-flight tasks finish. Single sweep at the end.

Likely answer: depends on impl-overview-data-dynamic-stages-schema status. If it's not yet spawned, do submodule FIRST (cleaner). If it's mid-flight, do submodule LAST. Surface this decision to operator during plan phase.

## Workflow

Concrete enough to skip /brainstorm-with-ralph (operator has chosen 'submodule' approach). Run /plan-with-ralph directly. Probably decomposes into 4-6 user stories (submodule add + path rewrite + spawn launcher pattern + memory update + CI invariant + docs).

No version bump required for codexu (it's a structural change, not a feature release). Single PR to main. ai-developer-toolkit itself untouched."

actions.prompt:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "How should we break down .ralph-overview/data.json so the overview-bookkeeper lead does NOT need to load the full task list into context every session, while preserving the bookkeeper's hand-edit ergonomics + the watcher's single-source-of-truth model?

## Why this matters

Today .ralph-overview/data.json is ONE monolithic ESM file with `window.OVERVIEW_DATA = { tasks: [...], runs: [...], workstream: {...}, ... }`. At ~50 tasks (current state), it's ~1200 lines / ~80KB. Every overview-bookkeeper Claude Code session auto-loads it via CLAUDE.md context. Every dashboard render parses + ships all tasks[] to the browser. Every MCP tool reads from the merged snapshot which contains the full list.

Projected scale: codexu's roadmap has Phase 1-6 with sub-tasks that could push this to 200-500 task entries within a year (shipped + in-flight + planned + closed). At 200+ entries the context-load alone becomes a significant fraction of an Opus context window, and the bookkeeper's reasoning quality degrades as it scans irrelevant entries to find the few that are actionable.

## Constraints / non-negotiable invariants

1. **Hand-edit ergonomics.** The bookkeeper edits .ralph-overview/data.json by hand (Edit tool, sometimes in a worktree). Whatever split must NOT require a complex multi-file write transaction per task. Atomic per-task edits.
2. **Single source of truth for an agent.** When an agent queries `overview.get_task(id)` or reads `overview-snapshot.json`, the result must be deterministic and capture the full per-task state. No N-file merge ambiguity.
3. **Watcher remains the sole writer of generated artifacts.** sync-ralph-state.mjs only writes overview-ralph-state.{js,json} / overview-snapshot.json / etc. It NEVER writes the hand-curated source(s).
4. **Static-build still produces a single self-contained overview.html.** The published artifact inlines whatever data the renderer needs; the split is invisible to end users.
5. **Backwards compatibility for at least 1 minor.** The current single-file shape continues to work; the split is opt-in.

## Candidate approaches to lens against

The brainstorm should pressure-test at least these candidate directions (the lens doesn't need to pick one — synthesizing a hybrid is fine):

### A — Per-task files under tasks/

One JSON (or markdown-frontmatter) file per task at `tasks/<id>.json` or `tasks/<id>.md`. The bookkeeper edits one small file per task; sync-core walks the directory to assemble the snapshot. CLAUDE.md auto-loads only an INDEX (slug + title + status + lastTouchedAt — maybe 5-10 lines per task) instead of the full content. Bookkeeper reads full task detail via Read on demand.

Pros: minimal context auto-load; atomic per-task edits; git history per task is cleaner.
Cons: needs a stable assembly script; loss of inter-task locality (currently bookkeepers see related tasks together in the file); risk of file-name collisions; needs new ESM bootstrap for the renderer.

### B — Lazy MCP tools

Keep the single file but never auto-load it into CLAUDE.md context. The bookkeeper queries via MCP tools (`overview.list_tasks({filter})`, `overview.get_task({id})`) for only the tasks it needs in the current turn. The full data lives on disk but is invisible to the model unless asked.

Pros: zero file-system restructuring; the existing single-file ergonomics stay; immediately deployable via MCP tool additions.
Cons: requires discipline (model has to remember to query); silently breaks when the model assumes 'it's all in context'; doesn't help dashboard load weight.

### C — Lifecycle-bucketed files

Split by lifecycle: plans/overview-data-active.js (tracked/planning/implementing) + plans/overview-data-shipped.js (merged) + plans/overview-data-archive.js (archived). Bookkeeper auto-loads only -active.js. Shipped/archived loaded on demand.

Pros: simple split; matches the 'I only need to see in-flight work today' use case; merging into one source is straightforward.
Cons: bookkeeper has to remember to flip a task across files at ship time (a manual atomic-rename); cross-file references (spawnedFrom, dependencies) need stable IDs.

### D — Compression / summary projection in CLAUDE.md

Keep one file but auto-load only a SUMMARY projection in CLAUDE.md context: per task, drop the planPrompt/prompts text (often the biggest field) and keep only metadata (id, scope, lifecycle, lastTouchedAt, mergeCommit, descriptionHtml first line, warnings summary). The bookkeeper reads the full .ralph-overview/data.json on demand if it needs prompt detail.

Pros: zero structural change; the projection is a single script that the CLAUDE.md `@/plans/overview-summary.md` directive auto-loads; preserves the single-file edit model.
Cons: the projection has to be kept in sync (watcher-generated artifact); doesn't help the dashboard's full-tasks payload; just defers the problem (still O(n) per session).

### E — Hybrid: per-task files + assembled snapshot for renderer

Bookkeeper hand-edits tasks/<id>.json or tasks/<id>.md (cleanest format TBD); the watcher assembles `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json` which the React app reads. The hand-curated single file `.ralph-overview/data.json` becomes derivable from the per-task files. CLAUDE.md loads only an INDEX.md (auto-regenerated by the watcher) listing slug → title → status → 1-line summary.

Pros: combines A + D's benefits; renderer is unchanged (still reads a single snapshot); CLAUDE.md context is bounded regardless of task count.
Cons: most work; needs a clean format for the per-task source (markdown + frontmatter, JSON5, TOML?); needs migration tooling to convert today's .ralph-overview/data.json → tasks/<id>.* files.

### F — The 'no, the model just deals with it' lens

Devil's-advocate: 1M-context Opus + good attention means even 500 tasks at 200 LoC each (~100KB) fits in 5% of the window. The cost is real but not 'untenable'. Maybe the right answer is 'do nothing structural; let context cache handle it; revisit at 1000 tasks.'

Worth pressure-testing — if the lenses converge on F, the bookkeeper effort budget is better spent elsewhere.

## Deliverable

At the end of brainstorm Phase 5 (finalize), produce a `selected-direction.md` in `.ralph/brainstorms/overview-data-context-scalability/` capturing:

- Recommended direction (one of A-F or a hybrid).
- Concrete next steps (which approach gets a /plan-with-ralph follow-up; what work is deferred).
- Migration story (how today's .ralph-overview/data.json converts to the new shape; one-shot or incremental).
- Acceptance criteria for the eventual impl (how do we verify it works at 200+ tasks).
- Open questions for the operator that the planner should ask.

Do NOT chain into /plan-with-ralph from the brainstorm member. The bookkeeper spawns a fresh plan-overview-data-context-scalability member from the selected-direction.md per the phase-discipline rule.

## Reference reading

- D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph-overview/data.json (the file under discussion).
- D:/harness-efforts/codexu/plans/codexu-roadmap.md (downstream scale projection — what's coming in Phase 1-6 sub-tasks).
- D:/harness-efforts/codexu/CLAUDE.md (untracked bookkeeper operating manual — describes the auto-load + edit contract).
- ./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/CLAUDE.md (sync/watcher contract).
- ./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs (current assembly logic — where the split's assembly would slot in).
- ./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/lib/derive-next-command.mjs + crews-cross-walk.mjs (downstream consumers that read .ralph-overview/data.json).
- ./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts (OverviewData shape).
- Sibling overview-data tasks in flight: overview-data-dynamic-stages-schema (renames phase→lifecycle) + overview-data-ship-manifest (adds shipManifest field) — coordinate with both. Impl phase of this scalability work should land AFTER both, to avoid re-rebasing a per-task split mid-rename.

Lenses to deploy: feasibility (codex), product-reality (copilot), devil's-advocate (challenge: 'is the problem real today, or premature?'), simplification (does the proposed shape actually reduce cognitive load, or just spread the same complexity across more files?). Plus a Claude general-purpose lens reading the actual file sizes + token counts to ground the discussion in numbers."

actions.prompt:
/plan-with-ralph "Add structured ship provenance to OverviewTask. Today the bookkeeper writes a bare mergeCommit: string (sometimes comma-separated for multi-commit ships) and there's nowhere to record what each commit did or what the ship adds end-to-end. Operator wants the dashboard chip to surface a tooltip listing commit oneLines + a 1-3 paragraph summary, and agents querying the snapshot to get structured ship provenance.

## Design

**New OverviewTask field (additive):**

```ts
shipManifest?: {
  shippedAt: string;                  // ISO 8601
  summary: string;                    // 1-3 short paragraphs human-written; what shipped, key behaviors, anything operator-relevant
  commits: Array<{
    sha: string;                      // short (7-8 char) OR full; renderer accepts both
    oneLine: string;                  // first line of commit message (verbatim)
    repo?: 'codexu' | 'ai-developer-toolkit' | 'codex' | 'happy';  // omit for codexu (default)
  }>;
}
```

**Back-compat handling:**
- Keep the existing `mergeCommit?: string` field as an alias. Read-side: when shipManifest is present, prefer it; when only mergeCommit is present, render the bare SHA as before (no commits[] or summary). When BOTH present, shipManifest wins; mergeCommit acts as a hint for the leading SHA only.
- Writer-side: when the bookkeeper marks a task shipped, populate shipManifest (new path). Existing entries (the 8+ already shipped) can be left as-is with mergeCommit-only until backfilled.
- Drop mergeCommit one minor later (after backfill of shipped entries is done in a follow-up task).

**No watcher derivation in v1.** The summary is human-written — the bookkeeper composes it at ship time. Commits are also bookkeeper-captured (from the cherry-pick log + the impl member's final report). v1 does NOT try to derive commits/summary automatically; v2 could optionally derive commits via `git log <prevMergeCommit>..<newMergeCommit> --oneline` when given the SHA range. Out of scope for v1.

## Files to touch

**codexu repo:**

1. .ralph-overview/data.json — no immediate rewrite of existing entries needed; the schema accepts both mergeCommit-only and shipManifest-shaped entries. Optionally backfill 1-2 recent ships (plugin-scope-agents, ralph-overview-multi-mcp-v210, crews-review-mid-turn-v160) as exemplars during impl phase so future bookkeepers see the shape in-repo.
2. plans/codexu-roadmap.md — update 'Bookkeeper workflow at-a-glance' to capture shipManifest fields at the 'EDIT .ralph-overview/data.json' step.
3. D:/harness-efforts/codexu/CLAUDE.md (untracked; bookkeeper operating manual) — same: add 'Capture commits + write summary' to the ship checklist.

**ai-developer-toolkit repo (ralph-overview plugin):**

4. tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts — add the shipManifest field to OverviewTask interface; keep mergeCommit as @deprecated. Define the ShipManifest type (commits + summary + shippedAt).
5. tools/overview-viewer/src/components/TaskCommand.tsx — when shipManifest is present, render its `summary` in the existing description area (or as an expandable section), and list `commits[]` in the chip tooltip (replacing or augmenting the current mergeCommit link rendering). Each commit oneLine + repo should be a clickable github URL when feasible (operator can hand-curate a known-repo-prefix map in .ralph-overview/data.json if needed; out-of-scope v1).
6. tools/overview-viewer/src/components/Kanban.tsx — ship-stage card meta shows commit count badge (e.g. '4 commits' instead of '1 sha') when shipManifest present.
7. tools/overview-viewer/src/utils/filters.ts — extend getTaskSearchHaystack to include shipManifest.summary + commits[].oneLine so search hits across both. Optional but high-value.
8. tools/overview-viewer/src/__tests__/*.test.tsx — fixture updates: at least one shipped task with full shipManifest, at least one with mergeCommit-only (back-compat path).
9. scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs — pass shipManifest through unchanged into the merged snapshot. No derivation.
10. scripts/lib/emit-snapshot-schema.mjs — add the new field + nested shape to the emitted JSON Schema.
11. tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/get_task.ts — surface shipManifest in the get_task result. list_tasks can include `shippedCommitsCount` as a derived summary field.
12. README.md + CLAUDE.md in the ralph-overview plugin — document the field with one example.
13. CHANGELOG.md — next minor entry: 'OverviewTask.shipManifest — structured ship provenance; mergeCommit deprecated.'

## Bookkeeper workflow change

When the lead marks a task shipped (the 'EDIT .ralph-overview/data.json' step), the change is:

BEFORE (today):
```js
  phase: 'shipped',
  mergeCommit: 'abc1234',
  lastTouchedAt: '2026-05-27T...',
```

AFTER:
```js
  phase: 'shipped',  // or lifecycle: 'merged' after dynamic-stages-schema lands
  shipManifest: {
    shippedAt: '2026-05-27T...',
    summary: 'Short 1-3 paragraph description of what shipped — operator-facing.\n\nKey behaviors, follow-ups, anything load-bearing.',
    commits: [
      { sha: 'abc1234', oneLine: 'feat: US-001 - story title' },
      { sha: 'def5678', oneLine: 'fix: US-002 - other thing', repo: 'codex' },
    ],
  },
  lastTouchedAt: '2026-05-27T...',
```

The lead captures `commits[]` from the impl member's final report + `git log --oneline <prevMergeCommit>..<newMergeCommit>` after cherry-pick. The lead writes `summary` in the bookkeeping commit.

## Acceptance

- types.ts has ShipManifest type + OverviewTask.shipManifest?: ShipManifest field.
- React viewer renders summary + commits[] in tooltip/expander for shipped tasks with shipManifest; falls back to bare mergeCommit display when only mergeCommit is set.
- At least 2 recently-shipped tasks in .ralph-overview/data.json backfilled with shipManifest as exemplars (suggested: plugin-scope-agents, ralph-overview-multi-mcp-v210).

/plan-with-ralph "Build top-level-agent ↔ top-level-agent communication across THREE distinct scopes — design has to decide whether to unify them under one transport or distinguish them with different mechanisms.

Scope A — Cross-tunnel / cross-machine (codexu-specific). Two top-level sessions live on different daemons (e.g., laptop daemon + remote machine daemon, both paired to the same operator's GitHub identity). Today daemons are silo'd (single-user-per-process embedded happy-server per Sprint A); no cross-daemon routing exists. This is the hardest scope because there's no existing routing layer. Options: (i) re-introduce a relay (we explicitly deleted this — operator policy); (ii) use Microsoft Dev Tunnels as a P2P channel between daemons; (iii) operator's mobile app acts as the rendezvous broker. Surface this choice to operator BEFORE designing the wire shape.

Scope B — Same-machine, daemon-managed. Two top-level sessions on ONE daemon. Daemon already coordinates via Socket.IO event-routing (packages/happy-server/sources/app/events/eventRouter.ts). The cross-session message-pass would extend that with a per-session inbox + a tool the agent invokes. This is the easiest scope.

Scope C — Parent-spawned-child relationship. An agent-spawner (from plugin-scope-agents) spawned the child top-level session; the parent retains a 'session reference' or capability. Communication has implicit trust + a known channel from spawn time. Could be a strict subset of B/A but with stronger invariants (e.g., parent can read child's logs/state; child can post back to parent's inbox without explicit handshake).

The design must answer: are these three separate mechanisms (different MCP servers / RPC surfaces per scope), one unified transport with scope-aware routing (single MCP with a 'scope' parameter), or a spectrum (parent-child piggybacks on B; B uses daemon Socket.IO; A needs the explicit cross-daemon design)?

Two consumer-facing channels to cover regardless of scope: (1) SPAWNING — request another top-level agent be spawned with role/cwd/plugins; (2) MESSAGE PASSING — request-response or pub-sub between live sessions.

Read plans/agent-view-research.md, plans/channels-research.md, plans/agent-view-followups.md if exists, codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/multi_agents_v2/ for codex's existing inter-agent plumbing (READ-ONLY per minimize-conflict-surface). Read packages/happy-server/sources/app/events/eventRouter.ts for the existing fan-out primitive that Scope B would extend.

Acceptance: design doc + per-scope working fixture: (B) two sessions on the same daemon exchange a message; (C) a spawned child reports back to its parent without re-handshake; (A) the design names a concrete transport choice for cross-daemon (no full implementation required for the first pass). Tests: vitest fixture for each scope. Pitfall: cycle-prevention applies across scopes (A spawns B spawns A → loop); need hop counter + operator-approval gate. Surface ARCHITECTURAL CHOICES (relay-vs-P2P-vs-broker, unified-vs-separate transports) to operator BEFORE landing code."

actions.prompt:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Long-horizon (v2/v3, 6-12 month) async-events architecture brainstorm for codexu / codex / crews / agent-comms. The short-term direction D-002 (durable mailbox + channel wake) was selected on the sibling async-events-design task 2026-06-02 -- this brainstorm builds FORWARD from D-002, NOT re-litigates it. Treat D-002 as the foundation; explore the next 3 layers above it.

## Scope axes to brainstorm

1. Producer ecosystem -- D-003 (channels-first Node producer hub in happyMcpStdioBridge.ts with git/fs/timer producers) vs D-004 (pilot first with measurement) vs hybrid (per-producer-class decision) vs none-needed (consumers self-emit). Frame: what should the v2 producer story look like? Who builds producers, where do they live, how are they discovered.

2. Subscription transport -- app-server-native subscription RPC (codex-side, persistent, deterministic) vs Node-process producer hub (Node-side, file/MCP wire) vs both-with-bridge. Frame: which producers live on which side of the wire and why?

3. agent-comms Scope A (cross-tunnel) -- D-002 explicitly leaves Scope A blocked. What's the v2 path? Encrypted relay model? Cross-tunnel notification fan-out? Per-machine subscriber directory? Required happy-server schema changes.

4. codex-as-crews-engine wire-protocol -- D-002 rejected channels-native crews storage but left the channels-leveraged hybrid (lead writes to file mailbox + MCP server emits McpServerNotification waking codex member's prompt queue) as a candidate. Frame the v2 wire-protocol concretely: what notification kinds, what mailbox-event semantics, what acknowledgment / replay path.

5. codex-app-server idle-timeout interaction -- D-002 + persistent subscribers raise the pressure on the app-server idle-timeout question (subscribers want app-server to outlive client disconnects). How does the v2 lifecycle answer that?

6. Heartbeat + presence -- across crews lead/member + agent-comms + multi-device, how does liveness / 'I'm here / I left' work? Today crews uses a file heartbeat on manifest.json; happy-server has a directory entry for tunnels. v2 should converge those or explicitly keep them separate with rationale.

7. Replay / catch-up semantics -- when a subscriber misses notifications (disconnect, restart, crash), how do they catch up? Mailbox-as-source-of-truth handles this for crews; what about app-server subscription RPC? Synthetic events from app-server state on reconnect?

## Adjacent in-flight context

- D-002 implementation is the immediate next step on async-events-design and will be a plan-with-ralph follow-up
- agent-comms (status=blocked) Scope B+C now have a pattern (D-002); Scope A is the lifeblood of this northstar
- 3d-workers (status=blocked) is blocked on 3a-skills/3b-agents prerequisites, NOT on channels; mentions of 3d-workers should note it's tangential
- codex-app-server-idle-timeout (status=ok, tracked) has its own brainstorm prompt; this northstar should coordinate but not subsume
- The unfilled informal codex-as-crews-engine task came up in operator chat 2026-06-02 19:55Z; this northstar should produce concrete enough material that filing it as a real task becomes mechanical

## Deliverable shape

Use the brainstorm skill's full lens process (codex feasibility + devils-advocate + copilot product-reality if reliable, else partial mode). Produce: recommendedDirection (or multiple competing directions for explicit operator-pick if convergence isn't clean), per-axis assessment for the 7 axes above, explicit list of v2-blocked-on-v1 dependencies, explicit list of v1-decisions-that-become-irreversible (so we can avoid those in D-002 impl), and a candidate-task list for what to file next post-brainstorm (e.g., 'file plan for app-server-subscription-rpc' or 'file brainstorm for cross-tunnel-notification-fanout').

NOT in scope: re-litigating D-002; specifying the D-002 impl (that's a separate plan-with-ralph); any UI / kanban-viewer changes; codex / happy / app-server source code changes (this is design-only)."

/brainstorm-with-ralph codex-app-server-daemon-codexu-integration

Context:

The codex app-server daemon is the runtime that codexu (happy-cli + happy-server) connects to for codex sessions. Today the integration is minimal and reactive — when a happy-cli session needs codex, it spawns a fresh app-server subprocess; when the happy-cli disconnects, the daemon's lifecycle behavior is undefined. The operator (2026-06-04) flagged this as an area where codexu support could be materially better.

Known tracked-task neighbors:

- `codex-app-server-idle-timeout` [brainstorm-only, codex|codexu] — single open question: when the last happy-cli client disconnects from a running codex app-server daemon, how long before the app-server exits? Today: undefined / undocumented behavior. Parked since 2026-06-03 without progression to plan.

- `agent-comms` [blocked, plan, codexu] — "Top-level agent ↔ top-level agent comms across 3 scopes (cross-tunnel / **same-daemon** / parent-child)". The same-daemon scope is the same surface this task is about; this task is more codex-daemon-specific while agent-comms is comm-protocol-general.

- `async-events-design` [brainstorm/plan/impl ready, codexu] — re-blocked 2026-05-14 waiting for channels primitive. Touches how codex daemon events would surface to multiple happy-cli clients.

- `async-events-northstar-architecture` [MERGED, codexu|codex] — long-horizon architecture brainstorm; already shipped. Re-read for context.

Gaps NOT tracked today (plausibly worth filing as separate tasks after this brainstorm converges):

1. **Daemon supervision.** Auto-restart on crash, health probes (`/healthz` style or codex-protocol probe), structured exit codes, restart-rate-limiting to prevent crash-loops. Who owns supervision — happy-cli, happy-server, or a new sibling supervisor? On Windows, what's the analog of systemd / launchd?

2. **Daemon discovery from happy-cli.** How does a fresh happy-cli session find a running codex app-server daemon vs. spawning one? Lock file? Named pipe? Local-only socket? Cross-machine via tunnel (when happy-server is remote)? When two happy-cli processes start near-simultaneously, do they race or coordinate via a lock?

3. **Multi-client multiplexing.** Can multiple happy-cli sessions share ONE codex app-server daemon? Today: each happy-cli probably spawns its own. The multi-client case: happy-server's remote codex sessions + local happy-cli sessions on the same dev box both want codex. Sharing one daemon saves resources (Rust + V8 cold-start is ~1GB RSS, ~10-15s warm). But shared state introduces isolation questions: per-session conversation/context isolation, per-session auth.

4. **Daemon resource lifecycle.** Long-running daemons accumulate: conversation context, file handles for read_file/write_file tools, MCP server connections, in-memory caches. After what duration of idle should the daemon prune? Should there be a hard memory ceiling? Crash on exceed vs. graceful eviction? How does idle-timeout (existing task) compose with this?

5. **Daemon observability.** `codex daemon status` CLI command analog? Structured log emission to a sidecar file? Prometheus-style metrics endpoint? Per-session metrics (turn count, token usage, last-active-at)? Crash dump location? How does happy-server surface daemon health to the mobile app?

6. **Daemon-side identity/auth.** Does a happy-server-spawned codex daemon honor different OAuth than a happy-cli-spawned one? Multi-tenant: are codexu OAuth identities per-daemon or per-session? Token-refresh flow on long-running daemons.

Deliverable:

Multi-lens brainstorm (Codex feasibility + Copilot product-reality + Devil's advocate + Claude synthesis) → `selected-direction.md` ready for `/plan-with-ralph --from-brainstorm`. The synthesized direction should:

- Pick the TOP 2-3 gap areas to prosecute first (not all 6 — that's a multi-month tail).
- Identify which gaps are unblocked NOW vs. which need a prereq (e.g., supervision likely needs discovery first).
- Identify which gaps are real bookkeeper-driven impl-worthy items vs. which are just brainstorm-only "open questions" like the existing idle-timeout one.
- Identify any gap that's actually subsumed by `agent-comms` or `async-events-design` (avoid double-tracking).
- Identify any gap that's deferred to a future codex-fork refactor (e.g., daemon-side context sharing might wait for upstream rust-v0.140+).

DO NOT try to bundle all 6 areas into a single plan or impl. Output a list of N small follow-up tasks the bookkeeper should file after the brainstorm ships.

This feature MUST NOT log or persist customer data. shipManifest.summary:
Resolved the bug where codex crew members spawned via the crews `RUN: /<skill>` convention did not get the skill's SKILL.md body injected, so they implemented manually instead of running the multi-phase /implement-with-ralph workflow. Root cause (found on the 4th investigation pass): the engine-aware codex rewrite (`rewriteCodexSkillMention` in crews hooks/actors.js) used a non-global `.replace()`, so it rewrote only the FIRST `RUN:` regex match. Real-shaped spawn prompts contain an earlier prose `RUN:/<word>` mention (e.g. the literal 'RUN:/skill') that matches first, resolves to a non-ralph token, is returned verbatim, and short-circuits the replace before reaching the real trailing `RUN: /implement-with-ralph` directive. That is why bare-prompt unit tests and isolated argv captures passed while real codex spawns silently failed.

The fix (crews 3.18.0) scans globally for the first RESOLVABLE ralph mention, skipping earlier non-ralph prose mentions, and rewrites it to the namespaced `$ralph-orchestration:<slug>` form codex requires for SKILL.md injection. It adds real-shaped LF/CRLF regression tests plus a launcher-delivery integration test (minimal-prompt tests structurally could not catch the prose short-circuit); full suite 284/284. Validated end-to-end by a live codex dogfood (codex-cli 0.135.0-copilot-api.1) against the exact fixture that failed under 3.17.0: INJECTION=YES, full multi-phase SKILL.md body injected ('Phase sequence: 1 -> 1.5 -> 2 -> 2.5 -> 2.7').

Two earlier ships (3.16.0 sigil `/`->`$` swap, 3.17.0 namespacing) were necessary precursors masked by this separate non-global-replace bug. codexu records the ai-developer-toolkit submodule pointer bump to 59654f0b and the active-plugin-versions table update to crews 3.18.0. Operator directive in effect: members stay on copilot until the operator signs off on re-enabling codex-default now that the live dogfood passes.

PROBLEM: when the lead/bookkeeper reads listener output or review-mail results, the data is often large (proactive batches can be 20-30KB, saved to a temp file). The lead then reads only the head (`Select-Object -First N`) or greps, which can MISS a buried terminal report (done/question/blocked) sitting after many progress rows. This is a documented, repeatedly-hit failure mode (see crews/codexu memory 'review-mail parsing': a done was missed after 21 progress rows because the output was printed-then-truncated at 30; happened again multiple times in the 2026-06-09 session). WANT: a short OVERVIEW/SUMMARY describing the batch, emitted at the TOP / self-contained in the first ~15 lines, so a model reading only the head never misses an actionable message. Minimum content: total entry count, sender(s), counts by kind (done/question/blocked/progress/reply), and the ACTIONABLE (non-progress) entries listed FIRST with {seq, sender, kind, summary, reply-required}. Also consider enriching the listener delivery envelope (`{type:messages,count:N,...}`) with a kind breakdown so even the one-line listener wake flags actionable items. Plugin-side (crews) change. Make robust to head-only reads + add tests + version bump + marketplace-index sync.

kanbanCards.html: INVESTIGATION-first, URGENT (operator-flagged 2026-06-09). SYMPTOM: crews PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop hooks frequently fail with 'hook timed out after 5s' on codex members AND on the lead session; the lead's listener keeps getting reaped and re-arm/review tools get 'Denied by preToolUse hook (hook errored)'. ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (to confirm + measure): crews hooks run as a FRESH node subprocess per fire (codex fires PreToolUse+PostToolUse on EVERY tool call), each acquires withManifestLock + does an atomic manifest write. crews v3.5.0/v3.8.0 hardened atomic writes against Windows Defender/AV lock contention with a cumulative retry budget of ~6.5s (CREWS_RENAME_RETRY_LIMIT=10 x exp backoff 100/200/400/800..cap 1000ms in hooks/safe-io.js) PLUS isTransientLockOpenError retries (EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY/UNKNOWN) in hooks/locks.js. So a lock HOLDER's critical section can run LONGER than the engine's hard 5s hook timeout -> the engine kills the hook mid-retry, and every WAITER on that lock then blows its own 5s too. Amplified by N concurrent members contending the same .crews/ locks + per-hook fresh-node-spawn overhead saturating the box. NET: the AV-resilience budget (good intent) exceeds the hook deadline (bad outcome) -> the hardening that protects the LISTENER heartbeat path is TOO SLOW for the HOOK path. LIKELY FIX DIRECTION: make the lock/IO retry budget DEADLINE-AWARE -- the hook path (5s engine cap) needs a tight budget (~2-3s max, then fail-open) while the listener-heartbeat path can keep the full ~6.5s AV-resilience budget. Candidate immediate mitigation to evaluate: a hook-context env (e.g. CREWS_RENAME_RETRY_LIMIT lowered, or a new CREWS_HOOK_LOCK_BUDGET_MS) so per-hook lock/IO stays well under 5s. Also evaluate reducing per-hook critical-section work (do less under the lock; the heartbeat-only writes vs the full manifest write). RELATED (distinct surface, same class): crews-listener-silent-reap-across-idle-investigation (the lead listener reap is plausibly the SAME contention starving the heartbeat write). Plugin-side (ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews); fix is critical-infra (the hook layer gates everything) so investigation must pin the EXACT mechanism + a measured repro BEFORE any plan/impl. Files: hooks/safe-io.js (retry budget + knobs), hooks/locks.js (acquireLock + isTransientLockOpenError), hooks/mailbox.js (withManifestLock), hooks/pre-tool-use.js, hooks/post-tool-use.js, hooks/stop.js. Mandatory: do NOT weaken the AV-resilience on the listener-heartbeat path -- the fix must be deadline-SCOPED, not a blanket budget cut.

Investigation SHIPPED 2026-06-10 (.ralph/investigations/crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention/findings.md). Confirmed worst-case single contended hook = lock-acquire <=2s (locks.js:216-224, DEFAULT_MAILBOX_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS=2000) + atomic-write retry <=6.5s (safe-io.js:46, 100+200+400+800+1000x5) ~= 8.5s, past the 5s PreToolUse/PostToolUse cap; the 5s is CREWS-SELF-IMPOSED in .codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json (codex default would be 600s, discovery.rs:457) and hits BOTH codex AND Claude members (Copilot=30s, ~immune). OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-06-10: the timeout bump is a BAND-AID -- it happens WAY too often, which points at a deeper DESIGN bug. ROOT (re-centered): (1) ORPHAN-LOCK CASCADE -- when the engine kills a hook that blew its deadline, codex kill_on_drop (command_runner.rs:39) terminates the hook process but its .lock file PERSISTS and is NON-STEALABLE for 30s, so ONE slow write -> one killed hook -> an orphan lock that blocks EVERY subsequent hook on that manifest for 30s -> they all time out -> each killed -> each leaves another orphan lock = a self-sustaining 30s storm (this is the 'way too often'). (2) HOT-LOCK design -- the SINGLE actor-manifest lock serializes the ~10s heartbeat timer + every per-tool-call hook + (for leads) mailbox ops on the same file; one slow write starves everything behind it. This is ALSO why the lead listener keeps getting reaped (heartbeat write starved by a hook holding the lock -> stale heartbeat -> listener declared dead) -> SAME ROOT as crews-listener-silent-reap-across-idle-investigation. (3) TRIGGER frequency = Windows Defender real-time scan locking the rapidly-rewritten .crews files -> the 6.5s retry budget -> slow write -> first timeout. THREE-LAYER FIX: (L1 immediate no-code) add the .crews dirs to Defender exclusions; (L2 band-aid) bump the codex/claude hooks.json timeout; (L3 real fix) dead-holder lock-steal (record holder PID in the lock; a waiter steals immediately if isProcessAlive(holder)===false -> kills the 30s cascade) + do NOT run the slow atomic-write retry while holding the manifest lock + separate the heartbeat write from the hook write (so a slow hook can't starve the heartbeat -> fixes the listener reap too). (4) REDUCE PER-HOOK I/O + SYSCALL VOLUME (operator concern 2026-06-10: 'I dont want to also congest the system with system calls or file reads') -- INDEPENDENT of locking: every tool call spawns 2 fresh node hook processes (codex Pre+Post) each READING + atomically REWRITING (temp+rename) the manifest, the Stop hook READS the full events.jsonl transcript, and lock files churn (create/delete) per fire; under N members this is a flood of file ops that ITSELF invites the Defender locks. Coalesce/throttle manifest writes (don't rewrite on every hook -- only on real state change), avoid redundant full-transcript reads, and make the heartbeat a CHEAP lock-free stamp. Fewer file ops = less AV-lock surface = fewer slow writes AT THE SOURCE. The plan MUST center L3 (cascade + hot-lock + I/O-volume reduction), treating L1/L2 as mitigations -- NOT ship the timeout bump alone.

Plan shipped @ 619c965b (rebased onto main; pushed). Centers the REAL fix (not the timeout band-aid): (L3a) DEAD-HOLDER LOCK-STEAL -- record holder PID in the lock; a waiter steals immediately if isProcessAlive(holder)===false (kills the 30s orphan-lock cascade); (L3b) DON'T retry-under-lock (the ~6.5s atomic-write retry must not run while holding the manifest lock); (L3c) SEPARATE the heartbeat write from the hook manifest write (lock-free heartbeat stamp -> also fixes the listener reap); (L3d) REDUCE per-hook I/O+syscall volume (coalesce/throttle manifest writes, avoid full-transcript reads). L1/L2 (Defender exclusion done; bump hooks.json timeout) are mitigations only. PHASE-4 REVIEW SURFACED 2 HIGHS the IMPL MUST RESOLVE: (1) L3c is under-specified -- deriveListenerState(manifest) (actor-state.js:59-95) takes only the manifest object (no path/cwd), so reading a <actorDir>/heartbeat stamp needs an explicit API change + caller updates or a reader helper; (2) the file-op-count regression AC is under-specified -- must define WHERE the fs-op counter is wired (locks.js/safe-io.js/actors.js/mailbox.js) + which ops count.

DESIGN THE FIX (L3, the real one): (a) DEAD-HOLDER LOCK-STEAL -- record the holder PID in the lock file; in acquireLock, when the lock exists, check isProcessAlive(holderPid) and STEAL immediately if the holder is dead, instead of waiting the staleness window -- this kills the 30s cascade; handle the codex orphan-lock case where the holder pid is the killed hook process. (b) DON'T retry-under-lock: the slow atomic-write retry (safe-io.js writeJsonAtomicWithRetry, up to ~6.5s) must NOT run while the manifest lock is held -- either release the lock between retries or move the retry outside the critical section so a slow write can't pin the lock. (c) SEPARATE the heartbeat write from the hook manifest write so a slow hook can't starve the heartbeat (consider a dedicated heartbeat file / lock-free heartbeat stamp) -- this also fixes the listener reap. (d) REDUCE PER-HOOK I/O + SYSCALL VOLUME (operator concern, INDEPENDENT of locking): every tool call spawns 2 fresh node hooks (codex Pre+Post) each reading + atomically rewriting (temp+rename) the manifest, the Stop hook reads the full events.jsonl, and lock files churn per fire -- under N members a flood of file ops that itself invites the Defender locks. COALESCE/THROTTLE manifest writes (only rewrite on real state change, not every hook), AVOID redundant full-transcript reads (cache/seek the bg-detector), and use a CHEAP lock-free heartbeat stamp. Fewer file ops attacks the root (less AV-lock surface) AND reduces congestion. Measure the per-tool-call file-op count before/after. INCLUDE L1/L2 as mitigations: (L1) document the Defender-exclusion ops step for .crews dirs; (L2) bump the codex/claude .codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json + .github/plugin/hooks.json timeout to match Copilot's 30s (band-aid, heartbeat-safe). PRESERVE the AV-resilience on the listener-heartbeat path (do NOT just globally shrink the retry budget). Tests: a cascade-repro (a killed-hook orphan lock with a dead holder PID -> the next acquireLock STEALS it immediately, not after 30s) + a no-retry-under-lock assertion + the heartbeat-not-starved-by-a-slow-hook case. Plugin-side; version bump + marketplace sync + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md; two-commit submodule flow. Coordinate with crews-listener-silent-reap-across-idle-investigation (shared root) -- consider bundling. Full spec + the shipped findings.md are the source of truth."

kanbanCards.html: Filed 2026-06-10 (operator-flagged). BUG: crews `list-members` / `getMemberHealth` reports `pidAlive: true` for members whose tabs died DAYS ago (stale leftovers). Live evidence 2026-06-10: a list-members on crew ralph-pipeline showed 11 `pidAlive:true` members, but only 4 were genuinely active (started/last-turn within minutes); the other 7 had last turns 3000-21000 minutes (days) ago with dead wt tabs, yet still reported `pidAlive:true`. This FALSE POSITIVE misleads the bookkeeper's parallel-batch + load decisions and the operator's read of who's actually running. ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: per the 'Pid-first health' design, getMemberHealth (hooks/health.js) uses `<actorDir>/launcher.pid` as the primary tab-alive signal via a BARE liveness check (isProcessAlive(pid)). Two ways that goes false-positive: (a) Windows RECYCLES PIDs -- after the member's launcher pwsh exits, its PID gets reused by an unrelated process, so isProcessAlive(stale launcher.pid) returns true for the WRONG process; (b) the v1.2.12 deferred 'Hole #3' -- health.js still treats EPERM (unverifiable) as alive, so an inaccessible/foreign PID reads as alive. The launcher.pid file persists after the tab dies (nothing prunes it), so the stale PID lingers indefinitely. FIX DIRECTION: pidAlive must verify the PID is ACTUALLY THIS MEMBER'S LAUNCHER, not merely 'some process is alive at this PID'. crews ALREADY has the exact primitive: v3.6.6 `verifyLauncherRecycleSafety` (hooks/actors.js) confirms via CIM that a PID's image is pwsh.exe/powershell.exe AND its command line carries the spawn marker / launcher-script basename recorded in launcher.pid. Reuse that recycle-safety verification inside getMemberHealth's pidAlive determination (a recycled or foreign PID -> pidAlive:false). Optionally also demote to dead/quiet when the heartbeat is far past stale even if a verified PID looks alive. SECONDARY: treat EPERM/unverifiable as NOT-alive for the health surface (close the v1.2.12 Hole #3 for getMemberHealth specifically -- the stop-member recycle guard already fails-closed; health should too). Plugin-side (ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews); two-commit submodule flow + version bump + marketplace sync. Tests: a recycled-PID case (launcher.pid points at a live process whose image/cmdline is NOT this member's launcher -> pidAlive:false) + a genuinely-alive case + an EPERM/unverifiable case. Coordinate with crews-listener-silent-reap-across-idle-investigation + crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention (sibling health/liveness reliability tasks) but this is a DISTINCT surface (the pidAlive read, not the heartbeat write or the hook timeout).

kanbanCards.html: BRAINSTORM-first. Filed 2026-06-10 as the want-(b) follow-up recommended by the codex-notify-hook-async-bg-completion-investigation finding (.ralph/investigations/codex-notify-hook-async-bg-completion/findings.md). GOAL: give codex Claude-Code-parity non-blocking background-task UX -- the agent SPAWNS a long-running background process, ENDS its turn (operator keeps interacting), and the process COMPLETION surfaces ASYNC into the conversation as a later queued prompt -- WITHOUT the core-turn-loop surgery. WHY IT MATTERS: today `await_background_completion` is a BLOCKING in-turn await; while the model is parked in it the operator's messages QUEUE and completion does NOT surface async (operator-flagged 2026-06-09). KEY SOURCE FACTS (from the finding): (1) the fork ALREADY has a background-exit watcher `spawn_exit_watcher` (core/src/unified_exec/async_watcher.rs:114-183) that, when `Feature::BackgroundProcessNotification` is ON and the agent did NOT call the blocking await, queues a synthetic `<task_notification>` user message for the next turn + calls `maybe_start_turn_for_pending_work()` -- this IS the want-(b) primitive; (2) it's DEFAULT-OFF / under development (features/src/lib.rs:88-92, 740-746); (3) it's MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the blocking await -- both claim the same `notified` dedup flag (process_manager.rs:779-783, 800-810), so if the model parks in await_background_completion the watcher won't enqueue; (4) happy-cli's Option B substrate (McpServerNotification->prompt-queue: packages/happy-cli/src/codex/mcpNotificationConsumer.ts, mcpNotificationRouting.ts) is real but wired for MCP notifications, not unified-exec process exits, and also default-off. THREE CONFLICT TIERS from the finding: LOW = enable the existing default-off watcher + add a non-blocking spawn policy (short yield_time_ms so the agent turn ends; watcher queues completion later) + route through happy-cli's existing prompt queue -- stays in fork-owned unified-exec watcher/tool surfaces + happy-cli TS; MEDIUM = a new explicit non-blocking tool/param (exec_command(..., do_not_await:true, notify_on_completion:true) or subscribe_background_completion(session_id)) so the model can express 'surface completion later' without calling the blocking await; HIGH = modify the core session/turn loop so operator messages interleave while a tool awaits -- riskiest upstream-rebase surface, NOT recommended first. OPERATOR STANDING CONSTRAINT: minimize codex-fork upstream conflict surface -- so the brainstorm should lean LOW-conflict and rigorously justify if it ever recommends MEDIUM/HIGH. Brainstorm must settle: the exact non-blocking-spawn mechanism (yield_time_ms policy vs new param), how to avoid the dedup-flag mutual-exclusion (the agent must NOT call the blocking await for the same session), the feature-flag enablement story (BackgroundProcessNotification + the happy-cli routing flag), and the happy-cli wiring to surface a unified-exec completion (not just MCP notifications) into the prompt queue. Cross-repo: touches codex (codex-rs unified-exec + features) AND happy-cli (TS routing). Mandatory live validation at impl. Coordinate with the done investigation (read its findings.md first).

RECOMMENDED DIRECTION: LOW conflict -- enable the existing default-off Feature::BackgroundProcessNotification watcher + a spawn-then-end-turn policy + a race-proof turn-end wake. KEY FINDING (reframes the wiring): codex's watcher maybe_start_turn_for_pending_work() (tasks/mod.rs:567-593) AUTO-STARTS a real agent turn (start_task RegularTask) when the session is idle + the <task_notification> is queued -- this is codex-core-internal turn orchestration BELOW the app-server protocol layer, so in happy-cli's `codex app-server` mode the completion re-enters the model and emits turn events that app-server forwards WITHOUT happy-cli needing to inject a prompt. All 3 lenses (copilot + codex + devil's-advocate) leaned LOW. Cross-repo (codex + happy-cli), minimal happy-cli wiring. 3 files / 307 insertions.

US-001 codex seam CODE-COMPLETE (impl-codexseam, commit 7133aca92 on ralph/codex-nonblocking-bg-completion-surfacing in the inner submodule worktree): turn-end wake + INLINE-OUTPUT enriched wake payload (watcher already held a 1 MiB head/tail transcript buffer, read without draining + capped, mirroring the old await aggregation) + await_background_completion FULLY REMOVED.
