COMPILE-FIX CHECK-VERIFIED @ 6be476983f on ralph/codex-bg-seam-fix (2026-06-11). The blind-written code (7133aca92, never compiled) had a Send-bound flaw: the bg-completion watcher (a tokio::spawn'd Send task in unified_exec/async_watcher.rs) called the non-Send start_task directly via maybe_start_turn_for_pending_work (start_task is fine for its main-loop callers but cannot be hoisted into a Send task; SessionTask/AnySessionTask ARE Send+Sync so that was not the cause). VERIFIED: check --workspace clean; reverting the 7 fix files to HEAD^ reproduces the original non-Send error (tasks/mod.rs:503/594), proving the fix resolves it. THE WASTEFUL CYCLE: (1) mail arrives -> the active listener DELIVERS it + EXITS (listeners exit-on-delivery by design, v1.2.9); (2) now no active listener, so the lead's next tool call hits the arm-first PreToolUse gate (hooks/pre-tool-use.js) which emits the GENERIC 'BLOCKED: you must arm a background listener' block; (3) the lead arms -> the arm DELIVERS the pending mail + EXITS again -> next tool gated -> arm again ... a multi-turn, multi-token loop; only after the mail finally drains does the separate review-required nag surface the review-mail command. NET: when the REAL blocker is unreviewed pending mail, the hook tells the lead to ARM (which re-triggers the loop) instead of telling it to REVIEW-MAIL (the gate-exempt productive action that drains + advances the cursor). DESIRED: when unreviewed mail is pending (lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq, or pending mailbox entries exist), the PreToolUse block should surface the REVIEW-MAIL command as the PRIMARY instruction -- BEFORE/instead of the arm instruction -- so the lead drains first, advances the cursor, THEN arms against a clean mailbox (which stays blocking). review-mail is already gate-exempt, so this is a block-MESSAGE + gate-ORDER change, not a new capability. KEEP the arm-first SAFETY intact (members/leads still must arm; this only changes WHICH guidance is shown first when mail is the actual blocker). Consider: (a) in hooks/pre-tool-use.js, before emitting the generic arm block, check the review-required predicate; if unreviewed mail is pending, emit a 'review-mail first (then arm)' block instead; (b) make the arm-block message itself mention 'if you have pending mail, run review-mail first'. Files: hooks/pre-tool-use.js (arm-first gate), possibly hooks/stop.js + the review-required predicate (hooks/protocol/review-required.js) for the shared 'is there unreviewed mail' check. RELATED but DISTINCT: crews-listener-silent-reap-across-idle-investigation (a different reap cause -- idle, not delivery); crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention (the lock-starvation reap). This task is specifically the block-message ROUTING when mail is pending. Plugin-side (ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews); two-commit submodule flow + version bump + marketplace sync + tests asserting the review-mail-first block fires when unreviewed mail is pending and the plain arm block fires when it is not.

Plan shipped @ 9a1021ca (rebased onto main; pushed). Approach: in hooks/pre-tool-use.js, BEFORE the generic arm-first block, check the review-required predicate (lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq); when unreviewed mail is pending, emit a block whose PRIMARY instruction is the engine-aware REVIEW-MAIL command (reuse buildReviewMailCommand) + a secondary 'then arm' note; otherwise the plain arm block unchanged. Keeps arm-first safety. NOTABLE: the codex review lens caught a HIGH the Claude lens MISSED -- existing test review-gate.test.js:367-381 seeds review-required mail + listenerState:'exited' and asserts the plain arm block, so it WILL flip under the new behavior; the impl MUST update that test. (Copilot lens added 3 Medium refinements: test-helper trap, explicit engine matrix, byte-identical wording.) Multi-lens review earned its keep.

Evaluate: where to write, lifecycle/cleanup, size limits, how the agent reads it (a tool vs a path it cats), and how Claude Code / Copilot implement their truncation-spill UX (reference for parity). Keep fork-tenet-1 overlay where possible; minimal upstream-canonical seam.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed live 2026-06-11 by impl-knobb): a crew member that runs /implement-with-ralph spawns a `codex exec` ITERATION as a child process. That child INHERITS the member's CREWS_* identity env. The child's SessionStart hook then runs `crews.js arm <member-name>` under the CHILD's OWN (different) session id, CLAIMING the parent member's crew identity -- flipping the manifest (e.g. engine copilot->codex, sessionId -> the child's) and setting takeoverAt. After the hijack, the real member can no longer write its outbox (identity mismatch) so its done/question/blocked NEVER reaches the lead. The operator explicitly rejected engine-mismatch as the approach: "I dont think engine mismatch is the right approach, we might have the same engine." The real discriminator is "I am a NESTED CHILD PROCESS of a still-live member that holds this role under a different session id" -- which is engine-agnostic.

Integrating into the fork COLLAPSES that entire layer -- codex-rs already owns its turn lifecycle, approvals, and interrupts NATIVELY, so it does not need a JSON-RPC bridge to drive itself. What genuinely REMAINS to reach Happy is the smaller, well-defined Happy PROTOCOL CLIENT: E2EE (TweetNaCl on message bodies/metadata/state), happy-server Socket.IO connection, the @slopus/happy-wire session/message/metadata SCHEMAS (a shared, versioned protocol package -- a big help), session lifecycle (getOrCreateSession owns the keys), approval-to-mobile routing, and auth (GitHub device flow / Dev Tunnels connect token).

Transient/retryable; no actual crashes; but high friction + possible delayed crash-notification wake.

- The latch file is `liveness-notifications.json` (member-crash-notifications.js:77 LATCH_FILE_NAME='liveness-notifications.json'); its lock is `<that>.lock`.
- The default lock-acquire timeout is 2000ms (threads.js:94: `cfg.acquireLock(\`${file}.lock\`, Number.isFinite(timeoutMs) ? timeoutMs : 2000)`). Find EVERY acquireLock call on the liveness-notifications latch (member-crash-notifications.js + wherever the crash-sweep enqueues/reads it) and confirm the timeout + whether it passes the dead-holder-steal options.

Read that fix's code (the acquireLock/lock-steal helper it added) and determine why the liveness-notifications lock did NOT inherit it.

1. Apply the SAME dead-holder lock-steal (L3a) + a raised/backoff timeout to the liveness-notifications lock acquisition, so a dead holder is stolen immediately and live contention gets a longer budget. (Most consistent with the shipped fix.)
2. Make the crash-sweep liveness path LOCK-FREE or single-attempt-advisory (L3b/L3c style): the crash-notification latch is advisory; a failed acquire should be a NO-OP that logs + skips THIS cycle, NEVER an error that denies the member's tool. 3. Reduce contention frequency: the crash-sweep need not run on EVERY pre-tool-use of EVERY member — debounce/rate-limit per crew (e.g. one sweep per N seconds crew-wide) so N members don't each independently sweep+lock on every tool call.

Whatever the locking choice, the pre-tool-use hook must fail-soft on a sweep/lock error (log it, skip the sweep, ALLOW the tool). actions.label: Brainstorm
actions.prompt:
Brainstorm + design a FURTHER breakdown of the hand-curated overview store for human readability/navigation, building ON TOP of the hot/cold two-shard split that already shipped in ralph-overview 2.12.0.

VERIFIED STARTING POINT (re-confirm against source, cite file:line):
- ralph-overview >= 2.12.0 already splits the store into HOT `.ralph-overview/data.json` (tracked/active tasks + metadata) and COLD `.ralph-overview/data.archived.json` (merged + archived). The loader auto-detects single-file vs split and assembles the identical `{tasks:[...]}`; `data-edit` (mark-shipped/set-lifecycle) moves a task between shards under one store lock; `data-edit migrate-split` performs the partition. Find the loader, the shard-resolution, and the `migrate-split` verb in the ralph-overview plugin and cite them.
- ALL downstream consumers (the sync watcher, the MCP server, the React viewer, and the generated projections active-tasks.json / summary-projection.json / snapshot.json) consume the ASSEMBLED `{tasks:[...]}`. Any further split MUST keep that assembled shape byte-for-byte identical so every consumer is unchanged.

THE PROBLEM: even the HOT shard is large and hard for a human (and an agent loading it into context) to read/navigate. The operator wants it easier to read.

DESIGN OPTIONS to weigh (recommend ONE, with tradeoffs + a migration/back-compat path):
1. Per-SCOPE shards (e.g. `.ralph-overview/data/<scope>.json` for crews / codex / ralph-overview / happy / ...), assembled by the loader. Pro: a reader opens just the scope they care about. Con: cross-scope moves; scope is currently a per-task field, not a partition key.
2. Per-TASK files (a directory `.ralph-overview/data/tasks/<id>.json`), assembled by the loader. Pro: minimal diffs, trivially navigable, git-blame per task. Con: hundreds of files; loader must glob+merge deterministically; ordering.
3. Keep one file but improve READABILITY (stable key ordering, a generated human index `tasks/INDEX.md` already exists — extend it; or a generated per-scope read-only markdown/html view). Pro: zero loader change. Con: doesn't shrink the canonical file.
4. A hybrid: keep hot/cold for lifecycle, add a generated read-only per-scope or per-task VIEW (markdown/html) for humans while the canonical store stays as-is.

EVALUATE: the exact loader/assembly seam (file:line) and whether it can deterministically merge a directory of shards; how `data-edit` verbs (upsert-task/mark-shipped/set-lifecycle/add-kanban-card/set-prompts) would target the right shard; the invariant-check/CI implications; the `migrate-*` verb pattern already used; ordering/determinism so generated projections don't churn; and whether the win is worth the loader complexity vs. option 3/4 (generated views) which keep the store single-file. Cross-engine + agent-context-size angle (a smaller per-scope read is the real agent win).

DELIVERABLE: recommended direction (which option + why), the loader/assembly + data-edit seam (file:line), a migration verb sketch (mirroring migrate-split), back-compat for existing single/hot-cold layouts, and a test plan. actions.label: Brainstorm
actions.prompt:
Decide the correct behavior when a PERSISTED Anthropic model selection and the Anthropic gate (--enable-anthropic / features.anthropic_models / env var, default OFF) get out of sync.

THE BUG (operator-reported 2026-06-10, hit live on the .3 build): the active model PERSISTS across runs (saved in session/config state) but the gate does NOT. So if a user enables anthropic + selects an Anthropic model (e.g. claude-opus-4.8), then runs AGAIN WITHOUT the flag, the persisted model is still claude-opus-4.8 while the gate is OFF -> the model is routed through the default Responses API path, which Anthropic models do not support. Every message then fails until the user manually changes the model. Exact operator output:
    WARN Model metadata for `claude-opus-4.8` not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata; this can degrade performance and cause issues.
    ERROR {"error":{"message":"model claude-opus-4.8 does not support Responses API.","code":"unsupported_api_for_model"}}

YOUR JOB: produce a recommended direction (plus a runner-up) for how codex should handle this scenario. This is a genuine design question -- EVALUATE each option feasibility against the SOURCE; do NOT rubber-stamp. Candidate directions to weigh (add others you find):
  (A) Persist the gate too -- if --enable-anthropic was used, persist features.anthropic_models so later runs keep Anthropic routing. (Is persisting a transient flag idiomatic for codex config? where is the active model persisted today?)
  (B) Model-selection implies the gate -- if the persisted/active model is an Anthropic model, auto-enable Anthropic routing (the model choice IS the signal). Risk: silently re-enabling an experimental feature.
  (C) Startup guard / self-heal -- on startup, if (persisted model is Anthropic) AND (gate OFF): either (c1) reset model to a safe Responses-API default, (c2) hard-error EARLY with a clear actionable message instead of failing per-message, or (c3) prompt the user.
  (D) Gate controls AVAILABILITY -- when the gate is OFF, Anthropic models cannot be selected OR persisted (picker hides them; any persisted Anthropic model is treated as unset/reset to default).
  (E) Route by model capability, not by gate -- dispatch already knows claude-* must use ChatCompletions (the .3 text-fix added AnthropicSseParser); key routing off the model declared API-support so a claude model ALWAYS routes ChatCompletions regardless of the gate, and the gate only controls whether claude models are OFFERED.

REQUIRED SOURCE INVESTIGATION (cite file:line): (1) where the active model is persisted across runs (session state / ~/.codex/config.toml / rollout); (2) where the gate is resolved (codex_copilot::anthropic_models_enabled() + the .3 --enable-anthropic flag / features.anthropic_models -- see task codex-anthropic-enable-flag, commit 2602c5474); (3) the dispatch that chooses Responses vs ChatCompletions and where "does not support Responses API" / "unsupported_api_for_model" is raised (model-provider crate; copilot_models_endpoint.rs); (4) whether per-model API-capability metadata exists (the "Model metadata for claude-opus-4.8 not found" warning suggests a metadata lookup that misses when the gate is off).

CONSTRAINTS: keep Anthropic support OPT-IN/experimental (do NOT silently enable a half-baked feature for all users) while making the failure mode non-confusing. Prefer the smallest change that eliminates the per-message-failure trap. Note the upstream-conflict surface (fork-only copilot-api behavior). Recommend whether this BLOCKS the .3 release or is a follow-up.

This is the codex inner submodule (read-only analysis). Commit a brainstorm.json under .ralph/brainstorms/codex-anthropic-model-persists-without-enable-flag/. Report kind=done with the recommended direction + whether it is a .3 blocker.

Copilot/claude member tabs DO get renamed correctly. ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: the codex launch path lacks anything that MAINTAINS the tab title. Per crews v3.6.0 codex support: (a) spawnMember stamps the wt.exe `--title '♙ <name> (<crew>)'` at tab creation (engine-agnostic), BUT (b) codex gets NO `--name` flag (codex has no --name), and for copilot/claude it's the engine's `--name`-driven OSC title emission that KEEPS the tab renamed for the session lifetime; AND (c) the codex launcher passes `-c tui.terminal_title=[]` which DISABLES codex's own per-turn TUI title rewriter (added so codex wouldn't CLOBBER the wt --title). (Compounded by codex 0.135's ~60-90s startup, during which only the launcher pwsh is up.) /brainstorm-with-ralph Brainstorm a new SKILL for the ralph-overview plugin that IMPORTS an existing roadmap document from a user's repo and converts it into the .ralph-overview/data.json task format we use for ralph-orchestration.

## What it does
Take a human-authored roadmap artifact already living in a repo -- a ROADMAP.md, a TODO.md / backlog doc, a checkbox task list, a markdown table of features, or a set of GitHub issues (via gh CLI) -- and produce validated tracked tasks in data.json (each with id, scope, lifecycle=tracked, status, lastTouchedAt, the cmd-warn problem-statement kanban card, and optionally a stage seed for brainstorm/plan/impl).

## Design questions to lens against
(1) INPUT FORMATS: which to support first (freeform markdown headings/bullets, checkbox lists `- [ ]`, markdown tables, GH issues). How robust must parsing be vs. asking the user to point at a section.
(2) MAPPING: how to map a loose roadmap line to our schema -- id slugging (collision-safe), scope inference (heuristic vs ask), problem-statement card authoring from the roadmap text, when to emit a stage seed vs leave it for later.
(3) AMBIGUITY: underspecified items -- ask interactively vs best-effort-with-flag. How much to infer.
(4) DEDUP: detect items that already map to an existing task id (don't double-file). Across BOTH hot + cold shards.
(5) CORE REUSE (operator-fixed): MUST reuse the shared id-scoped, atomic, invariant-checked mutation core that backs `node tools/data-edit.mjs upsert-task` (the plugin lib the MCP write tools call), NOT a fresh re-implementation. WRITE-ONLY automation: validated upsert + JSON-parse + task-count + dup-id guards + print a diff for confirmation; does NOT git stage/commit/push (lead/operator owns git side-effects).
(6) CROSS-ENGINE: Claude Code + Copilot CLI, like the other ralph-overview skills (/triage, /work-on, /blocker-report, /expand-task).
(7) RELATIONSHIP to ralph-overview-create-task-skill (interactive SINGLE-task creation): this is the BULK/IMPORT sibling. Decide whether they share a common core/flow or are cleanly distinct skills, and how to avoid duplicated logic.

DESIGN the skill: the slash-command name + surface, the input-detection/parsing flow, the field-mapping + ambiguity-resolution UX on both engines, the dedup strategy, and the exact reuse seam into the shared mutation core. Pick a recommendedDirection and analyze the conflict surface (which plugin files it touches, overlap with create-task-skill).

kanbanCards.html: Filed 2026-06-08 by operator request. CONTEXT: the agent-comms design (plans/agent-comms-design.md §5 "Scope A", shipped with task agent-comms @ 2a47a29c, plan @ a2e0f0ed) already pins cross-machine session discovery + transport on Microsoft Dev Tunnels END-TO-END (data + signaling + rendezvous + discovery + auth), with NO central happy-server broker/relay -- discovery via 'devtunnel list --json' (the Dev Tunnels management plane IS the per-identity registry, machines keyed codexu-<hostname>). The ONE remaining "server" is the EMBEDDED per-daemon happy-server that hosts the Scope A ingest sink (POST /agent-comms/ingest) because the loopback control server is bound to 127.0.0.1 and cannot accept tunnel traffic (§5.2). OPERATOR GOAL: drop EVEN the embedded per-daemon happy-server -- discovery AND ingest done purely over Dev Tunnels with no happy-server at all. OPEN QUESTION for the brainstorm member to settle against SOURCE: what minimal tunnel-facing listener replaces the embedded happy-server (a tiny daemon HTTP listener in happy-cli; rebinding/extending the loopback control server to a tunnel-accessible port; the codex app-server itself; or a raw socket), while PRESERVING the §5.4 two-layer auth (operator-tunnel-ownership connect-token at the gateway + TOFU Ed25519 peer-pinning + ECDH-sealed body) and the hard requirement that Dev Tunnels stays the SOLE channel (nothing via phone/app/central server/relay). Note: Scope A live cross-machine networking was DEFERRED at agent-comms ship (design+skeleton only; §5.6) and was never re-filed as a follow-up -- this task also covers that gap. Related: codex-raw-session-happy-daemon-autoconnect (raw-session discoverability). Scope = codexu (happy-cli daemon/tunnelManager + happy-server embedded ingest). Research is delegated to the brainstorm member; not pre-judged.

actions.label: Implement
actions.prompt: Impl server-side device-key registration for the single-user public happy-server (feature remote-connectivity-single-user-public-evyatar-server, Phase 1 @ e9b0a152 + US-006 @ 9dd2a1a5 + US-007 @ e43c1c19 shipped). THE GAP (from US-007): the happy-app sends deviceEd25519PublicKey + deviceKeyId to /pair/complete, but happy-server pairRoutes.ts /pair/complete uses a zod .object() that strips unknowns and never persists the device public key. The Phase-1 verifier (packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/auth/remoteDeviceAuth.ts) checks device proofs against a PublicAuthConfig.devices list that US-006 buildPublicMode() starts EMPTY intending /pair/complete to enroll the first device. So the loop is broken: enrolled device's key is never pinned -> verifier has nothing to match -> device can't authenticate. FIX: (1) extend the /pair/complete request schema to accept deviceEd25519PublicKey + deviceKeyId (validate shape); (2) inside the operator-window + valid-QR-secret path (do NOT weaken that gate), TOFU-pin the device public key into the verifier's authorized-devices set (persist it in the per-daemon machine state/public-auth store the verifier reads); (3) make the persisted device set the source of truth the remoteDeviceAuth verifier checks against (so subsequent device-proof requests from that device succeed, and un-enrolled keys still fail closed); (4) add a spec proving: enroll-then-authenticate succeeds end-to-end, an un-enrolled device key fails closed, and enrollment still requires the operator window + QR secret. ALSO decide the socket transport-fallback nonce issue US-007 flagged: the app builds one nonce shared across ws+polling extraHeaders; a ws->polling fallback would re-send the same nonce and the server's single-use-nonce check rejects the 2nd as replayed_nonce -- either document reconnection:false as required, or allow a per-transport nonce / a bounded single-handshake exception. Scope: happy-server (+ happy-cli persistence if the device store lives there; + happy-wire if the /pair/complete schema is shared). Keep Dev Tunnels/loopback unchanged. Worktree in codexu. cargo N/A (TS). Run happy-server typecheck + full suite + the new enroll-then-auth spec.

Operator direction (2026-06-27): build a SINGLE-USER (single-tenant) happy-server exposed PUBLICLY on the operator's own evyatar.dev domain (e.g. happy.evyatar.dev or a subdomain) as the remote-session transport, secured the way Happy already works -- QR-code device pairing + end-to-end encryption -- so that public exposure is SAFE. This REPLACES the same-LAN D-001 approach (task remote-connectivity-lan-known-devices-additive-transport, now shelved): a secured public endpoint works REMOTELY from anywhere, not just on the same Wi-Fi, and an OUTBOUND-ONLY tunnel (e.g. Cloudflare to evyatar.dev) sidesteps the operator's corporate policy block on Microsoft Dev Tunnels (no inbound ports, no Microsoft).

KEY CONSTRAINT -- SINGLE USER, not multi-tenant: unlike the Happy UPSTREAM server (which serves many users isolated by their keys), this instance serves ONLY the operator. That simplifies the trust model (no multi-tenant data isolation), but the server is PUBLICLY REACHABLE so it MUST be hardened against public abuse: the QR-pairing + E2E model is the security boundary, there must be NO open self-enrollment, and the known concrete bypass (the currently-UNAUTHENTICATED /pair/complete route, pairRoutes.ts:59-119, source-verified in the prior LAN brainstorm) MUST be closed before anything is publicly exposed.

BRAINSTORM SCOPE (investigate + recommend; VERIFY feasibility + the security model rigorously -- do NOT rubber-stamp; public exposure is a real attack surface):
1. CURRENT STATE (source-verify, cite file:line): how Happy's QR-pairing + E2E encryption work today (happy-app pairing.ts, the Ed25519/X25519 TOFU key material, the server pairing routes + Socket.IO handshake, assertOperatorIdentityGate at happy-server index.ts:101-108), and how the per-daemon happy-server is currently reached. Reuse the prior LAN brainstorm's source findings (.ralph/brainstorms/remote-connectivity-lan-known-devices-additive-transport/).
2. ARCHITECTURE: is the public endpoint the per-daemon embedded happy-server exposed via an outbound tunnel, or a thin separate relay? Single-tenant hardening. How the operator's devices discover + pair with it (QR). Reconcile with the distributed-per-daemon model (a single-user PERSONAL server is consistent with 'no shared multi-tenant broker').
3. PUBLIC-EXPOSURE SECURITY (load-bearing): enumerate the attack surface of a public single-user server and prove the QR+E2E+pairing boundary is airtight -- close /pair/complete open enrollment, rate-limit, ensure every route + the Socket.IO handshake is fail-closed to non-paired devices, E2E so the tunnel/relay can't read session data. The decisive acceptance test: a hostile internet client that reaches the public URL cannot self-enroll, create a session, enumerate routes, or read any plaintext.
4. TRANSPORT: outbound-only tunnel to evyatar.dev (Cloudflare named tunnel, or alternatives) so it works behind corp policy; DNS/cert on evyatar.dev; coexistence with / replacement of the Dev Tunnels default.
5. CONFLICT SURFACE + SELECTABILITY: happy-server (auth/pairing/public-exposure hardening), happy-cli (tunnel provider to evyatar.dev), happy-app (reuse existing QR/E2E pairing + custom-server-url), codex Feature gate + /remote on. Gate fork-divergent behavior via the codex experimental-features mechanism.
6. RELATE TO LAN (D-001): this replaces it; note which of the LAN plan's server-side crypto-auth analysis is reusable, and whether LAN stays as a niche offline fallback.

DELIVERABLE: a recommended direction (single-user public evyatar.dev server design + the QR/E2E security-boundary model + outbound-tunnel transport + selectability/feature-gating + conflict-surface analysis) + a feasibility GO/NO-GO with the public-exposure security verdict front and center. DECISIVE acceptance: a hostile internet client reaching the public URL is fail-closed rejected on /pair/complete (401, NO key material), every tunnel-only route, AND the Socket.IO handshake (websocket + polling). Plan shipped @ c3540edb. 5 stories (S1-S5). Recommended fix = Option B2: the daemon's own machine client presents the local X-Loopback-Capability token on the public Socket.IO handshake in public mode; the public listener accepts a valid capability OR a device proof (fail-through). KEY FINDING: routing the daemon to the loopback LISTENER (the task's first idea) would silently BREAK app->daemon RPC (spawn/stop/fork) because the two embedded listeners are independent io servers with NO Redis adapter (isolated RPC rooms). Also fixes a parallel latent session-client bug (apiSession.ts). Machine-socket URL chosen per-connection at daemonClient.ts tunnelSocketIOOptions:143 (shared helper). shipManifest.summary: Fixed the daemon's own machine + session sockets looping 'Connection error: Unauthorized' forever in public mode. Root cause: in public mode the daemon's co-resident embedded socket clients connect to the public/tunnel listener (127.0.0.1:<tunnelPort>) which required an Ed25519 device proof they cannot present. Fix (Option B2): the public Socket.IO handshake now ALSO accepts a valid local X-Loopback-Capability token (the 0600 per-start secret at paths.loopbackCap, never transmitted remotely) as a fast-path, falling THROUGH to the unchanged device-proof path when the capability is absent/invalid (remote clients still fail closed). Authorization is by secret possession only, never by remote address (cloudflared collapses remote traffic to 127.0.0.1 at the origin). Rejected the naive 'route the daemon to the loopback LISTENER' fix because the two embedded listeners are independent Socket.IO servers with no Redis adapter, so app->daemon RPC rooms would be isolated (spawn/stop/fork would silently break).\n\nVERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-05: rebuilt + restarted the daemon in public mode; the daemon log now shows '[API MACHINE] Connecting to http://127.0.0.1:51371 -> Connected to server -> Keep-alive started -> Daemon state updated successfully' with ZERO Unauthorized lines (was an infinite ~3s loop). 108 happy-server tests (socket.spec.ts +5 new S1) + 20 happy-cli tests (socketTunnelAuth +4 new S3/S4, daemonClient +1 new S2); US-005 route-inventory gate green; both typechecks exit 0.

shipManifest.summary: Fixed the Happy web app's realtime Socket.IO status badge latching at 'error' in public mode (single-user happy.evyatar.dev). Root cause (investigated live, HIGH confidence): the app requested transports ['websocket','polling'] (websocket FIRST) with reconnection:false and no tryAllTransports. Fix (packages/happy-app/sources/sync/socketOptions.ts public-mode branch): on web use transports ['polling'] (the transport that actually carries the CF + device-proof headers in a browser); native keeps ['websocket','polling']; both add tryAllTransports:true. reconnection:false + the single-use-nonce security model and the non-public (tunnel/loopback) branch are unchanged.\n\nVERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-05: restarted the expo-web dev server with the fix, reloaded the web app against happy.evyatar.dev; the realtime badge now shows 'connected' (green) where it previously showed 'error'. socketOptions.test.ts 7/7 (added web-polling + native-websocket + tryAllTransports assertions); happy-app typecheck exit 0. Source-audit the current input history, Up Arrow handling, pending steering and queued item APIs, `removeMostRecentPendingItem`, attachments, multiline input, slash commands, prompt modes, Ctrl+Q queue semantics, and pending UI updates in D:\harness-efforts\copilot-agent-runtime. Decide precise activation rules so recall does not break ordinary command-history navigation: for example, only when the input is empty and a user-authored pending item exists, with repeated Up Arrow optionally recalling additional pending items in LIFO order. Define whether steering and explicitly queued messages are both recallable, how batches/attachments/displayPrompt/model metadata are restored, how the queue item is removed atomically before editing, what happens if the user presses Escape or submits again, and how remote/multi-client sessions behave. Preserve ordering of remaining queued work and guarantee the recalled message is not simultaneously visible as pending or persisted twice. Search open issues and PRs before filing anything. Require focused SDK/state tests plus a real terminal E2E covering: queue multiple messages, recall the newest with Up Arrow, verify it leaves pending UI and appears exactly in the editor, edit and resubmit it, verify one final user.message, recall and discard another, and confirm normal Up Arrow history behavior when no pending item exists. Public descriptions may compare only externally observable Claude Code UX; do not mention internal source inspection or private implementation details.

kanbanCards.html: Fix multi-question Copilot CLI prompts so custom free-text answers survive backward navigation. Today a user can type a custom answer, advance to a later question, press Shift+Tab to return, and find the earlier text erased instead of available for review and editing. Each question's draft answer should be preserved independently until final submit or cancellation.

actions.label: Brainstorm
actions.prompt: Brainstorm a robust fix for Copilot CLI multi-question dialogs where a custom typed answer is lost after advancing and then navigating backward with Shift+Tab. Source-audit the ask_user/elicitation/multi-step form state model, question index transitions, custom-option/free-text input buffers, Tab/Shift+Tab handlers, validation, focus management, submit/cancel paths, remote responses, and dialog re-render/remount behavior in D:\harness-efforts\copilot-agent-runtime. Determine whether drafts are stored globally, reset on question change, or reconstructed incorrectly, and design per-question durable draft state that preserves exact text and cursor/editability when revisiting a question. Cover transitions between predefined choices and custom answers, toggling away from and back to Other/custom, required/optional questions, multiline text, validation errors, repeated forward/back navigation, mouse and keyboard paths, cancellation, and final payload correctness. Ensure drafts are cleared only when the dialog is definitively submitted or cancelled, not on navigation. Search open issues and PRs before filing anything. Require focused component/state tests and a real TUI E2E with multiple questions: type a custom answer in question 1, advance, enter an answer in question 2, Shift+Tab back, verify question 1 text and cursor are preserved, edit it, advance again, and verify final submission contains the edited answer exactly once. Include regression coverage that predefined selections and untouched questions continue behaving normally.

kanbanCards.html: Make Escape cancellation in Copilot CLI feel instantaneous. Today stopping model generation, shell commands, subagents, or related background work can take long enough that the UI appears unresponsive. Explore an immediate user-facing cancellation boundary that stops rendering/thinking state and restores control at once, while process termination, transport aborts, persistence, and cleanup complete safely in the background.

actions.label: Brainstorm
actions.prompt: Brainstorm how Copilot CLI can make Escape cancellation feel instantaneous while preserving correct cleanup in D:\harness-efforts\copilot-agent-runtime. Source-audit the full cancellation chain: terminal key handling and repeated-Escape semantics, foreground model/stream abort, Responses/WebSocket transport, tool execution, attached and detached shell process trees, Task/subagent cancellation, hooks, permission/ask-user dialogs, queued and steering messages, session state, event persistence, background notification generation, locks, and final UI re-render. Separate user-perceived cancellation latency from teardown completion. Evaluate a two-phase design where Escape immediately acknowledges cancellation, stops streaming/spinners, marks the foreground turn cancelled, restores the input field, and allows new interaction within a strict latency target, while idempotent cleanup continues asynchronously with visible task status and eventual completion notification. Define which work Escape cancels by default: current foreground turn only, child tools, attached background work, or all background agents; consider a second Escape or explicit escalation for broader cancellation. Compare externally observable Claude Code cancellation behavior as UX prior art, but do not mention internal source inspection or private implementation details publicly. Instrument latency milestones from keypress to visual acknowledgement, transport abort, process termination, queue readiness, and persistence completion. Account for Windows process termination, TTY applications, hung hooks, non-cooperative MCP tools, race conditions with natural completion, duplicate cancellation events, orphaned tasks, lost queued messages, and resume behavior after interruption. Search open github/copilot-agent-runtime issues and PRs before filing anything. Require focused state-machine tests and real terminal E2E scenarios with a slow streaming model, long shell command, background subagent, and hung/non-cooperative cleanup: Escape must visibly return control immediately, no further streamed content may appear, new user input must be accepted promptly, cleanup must complete exactly once, and no processes or pending UI rows may be leaked.
